items.title: Agha hits fourth ODI ton as Pakistan defeat Sri Lanka in tri-series opener
items.summary:
Salman Ali Agha made a triumphant return to the Pakistan team with his fourth ODI century in a 37-run victory over Sri Lanka in the cricket tri-series opener on Sunday.
Agha hit 107 off 90 balls and Pakistan scored 305 all out in 49.5 overs after Sri Lanka captain Kusal Mendis won his fourth successive toss and chose to field.
Agha was among seven Pakistan cricketers summoned back home at the end of August during a tumultuous tour of England after Agha had led the team in the first test.
Pakistan pace bowlers overcame heavy dew and threatening half centuries from Pavan Rathnayake (79) and Janith Liyanage (60) to dismiss Sri Lanka for 268 in 48.1 overs.
Captain Shaheen Afridi picked up 3-55 while Naseem Shah pinned down Sri Lanka's top-order with impressive swing bowling to finish with 2-43. Haris Rauf ran through the tail with 2-48 while seam all-rounder Faheem Ashraf grabbed 2-49, including the key wicket of Rathnayake.

The injury is also a blow for PSG coach Luis Enrique, given that Mendes would likely have marked Barcelona superstar Lamine Yamal in their Champions League game on Tuesday.
Yamal operates from the right flank and often cuts inside. The 19-year-old Yamal has scored nine goals overall this season for Barcelona, which has won all its 11 games so far in La Liga and Champions League, and has also been in terrific form for Spain.

items.title: Fire at Canada military base kills 4
items.summary: Alberta: Four Canadian service members were killed and 39 people injured, including 19 critically, when a fast-moving fire overtook soldiers conducting live-fire combat training at a military base in Alberta, officials said Sunday.Maj. Gen. Wade Rutland said military officials knew about the fire for hours but believed it was sufficiently contained to allow training to continue before winds suddenly shifted, sending flames racing toward the soldiers."The fire was a kilometer away when the wind shifted. That is not normal for a fire to move a kilometer in 36 seconds," he said at a news conference in Edmonton.Rutland said a commander at the scene told him soldiers went from seeing no fire to having flames upon them in less than a minute.The fire broke out Saturday during high-intensity combat training involving Charlie Company of the 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry.About 84 soldiers were split between a grenade range and an area where they practiced attacks on simulated enemy positions. The fire swept into the second training area.Rutland said investigators had not determined what ignited the grass fire.He said the battalion was preparing for rapid deployment to global crises and a mission to reinforce Canadian troops in Latvia next spring.The military identified those killed as Sgt. Morgan Wong of the Loyal Edmonton Regiment and Privates Shaun Farrell, Aidan Goulding and Hayden Lykkemark of the 3rd Battalion, Princess Patricia's Canadian Light Infantry. All four were serving with the battalion, based in Edmonton.Alberta Premier Danielle Smith said 39 people were receiving medical care. Sayeh Zielke, chief executive of Acute Care Alberta, said 19 were in critical condition, eight were stable and 12 were ambulatory and receiving treatment for less serious injuries.Smith said some suffered severe burns and could face weeks or months of intensive treatment.Prime Minister Mark Carney described the incident as one of the worst peacetime tragedies for Canada's military on domestic soil. He ordered flags lowered to half-staff on federal buildings nationwide.Carney said the families of those killed had been notified. Those affected included regular forces personnel, reservists and soldiers from bases across Canada.Hospitals respond to mass casualtiesAlberta health officials said patients were transferred from Wainwright to four hospitals - the University of Alberta Hospital and Royal Alexandra Hospital in Edmonton, Foothills Medical Centre in Calgary and Red Deer Regional Hospital.Alberta officials said they had lifted the "Code Orange" emergency activated at several hospitals Saturday night to mobilize staff and beds for the casualties.The response involved 22 ground ambulances, six airplanes and two helicopters, with assistance from neighboring Saskatchewan. Smith said all patients had been accounted for and no further patients were awaiting transport.Wainwright Mayor Bruce Pugh said the town's small hospital was not designed to handle a mass-casualty incident but praised local medical personnel.Rutland confirmed that military search-and-rescue technicians parachuted into Wainwright to reinforce the emergency response. Pugh said their red parachutes were illuminated by flares as they descended shortly before midnight.Cathy Keane, a mayoral candidate in Ontario, said her eldest son was among those critically injured. "As a mother, right now I need to be with my son and family," she wrote on Facebook, saying she was traveling to Alberta.Conservative opposition leader Pierre Poilievre, who represents the area in Parliament, visited Wainwright on Sunday and said he had heard accounts of people who ran toward the danger to help others and were now fighting for their lives in hospitals.Military invest igates fireRutland said the fire ignited in the military training area, where multiple exercises were underway, and spread rapidly in unusually strong winds.He said winds had been within normal operating limits for much of Saturday, generally below 50 kph (31 mph), before intensifying rapidly. Range controllers rely on weather reports to determine whether training can safely continue, he said.The fire crossed established firebreaks before being contained with help from municipal firefighters.The Canadian military said there were no indications of terrorism.Rutland said military investigators would examine the circumstances, including whether safety protocols needed to change. "If our protocols need to change, then they'll be updated," he said.The military typically convenes a formal board of inquiry after such incidents, Rutland said, cautioning that determining what happened would take time.Rutland said Charlie Company had been withdrawn from the training area and the rest of the battalion suspended training Sunday.The Royal Canadian Mounted Police said officers were called shortly after 4 p.m. Saturday following reports of a fire in the base's training area.Large areas of Alberta were hit by a windstorm Saturday, with gusts up to 100 kph (62 mph). The winds toppled trees, sent signs flying and pushed flames beyond the base into surrounding rural areas.By late Saturday, the Municipal District of Wainwright said the fire was being held and that property and critical infrastructure were protected. No evacuation order was issued for residents.CFB Wainwright is one of Canada's busiest military training bases, where soldiers prepare for combat operations.The fire also disrupted advance voting ahead of Monday's referendum on whether Alberta should begin a process that could lead to independence from Canada. Elections Alberta said the Wainwright Communiplex advance polling location closed early Saturday and election materials were transported securely.

items.title: Ukraine fires over 1000 drones at Russia
items.summary: Ukrainian strikes set an oil export terminal and a depot ablaze in St. Petersburg on Sunday as Kyiv launched more than 1,000 drones at Russia in one of its largest aerial attacks of the war.The strikes came as tensions between Kyiv and Washington deepened, with U.S. President Donald Trump criticizing Kyiv's attacks on Russian oil infrastructure and the prospect of further U.S. sanctions against Moscow still uncertain.Also read: Trump claims 'great progress' in Russia-Ukraine negotiations; accuses Zelenskyy of not making better deal 2 years agoTrump said Sunday that he decided to hold off on implementing new sanctions on Russia because he doesn't "want to do anything that will drive, foolishly, Russia away from the bargaining table."In a social media post, the U.S. president defended his Friday order to issue a waiver to prevent new sanctions from being placed on Moscow from bipartisan criticism that he was favoring Russian President Vladimir Putin's interests over those of Ukraine. Trump said he believed new sanctions would undermine negotiations to bring about a diplomatic end to the war in Ukraine."I can sign it later, or any time that I want!" Trump added of the sanctions.Trump also lashed out at Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, who has been critical of Trump's recent outreach to Putin, for launching strikes on Russian energy infrastructure during the conflict, claiming Zelenskyy "doesn't want to end this war."Zelenskyy: Waiving sanctions strengthens RussiaSpeaking on NBC's "Meet the Press" earlier on Sunday, Zelenskyy said waiving sanctions against Russia would strengthen Putin's war effort. He also said U.S.-Ukraine intelligence sharing had resumed after being "blocked for some period of time."Zelenskyy said that while he trusted Trump, siding with Moscow would be a tragedy and a "historic mistake" for Washington."People want to forget what's going on. But we can't give this possibility to forget, or to change reality, or to change the truth," Zelenskyy said. "We can't compare me and Putin. He's (an) aggressor. He occupied us. He killed adults and children, his soldiers. He's a terrorist. And that's why I hope that President Trump will be very clear with this position."Later Sunday, Zelenskyy said on social media that he had spoken with U.S. presidential envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner about the results of an Oct. 9 meeting between U.S. and Ukrainian negotiating teams in Miami, as well as "next steps in diplomacy."Two killed as Russia and Ukraine trade blowsOne person was killed and five others were wounded in the St. Petersburg attack, which sparked fires at the Petersburg Oil Terminal and the city's Ruchi oil depot, local Gov. Alexander Beglov said. A logistics center belonging to Russian retailer Ozon and a data center operated by Russian tech giant VK were also targeted, the companies confirmed.Russia's Defense Ministry said Sunday that its forces had destroyed 1,015 Ukrainian drones over 15 Russian regions, the annexed Ukrainian peninsula of Crimea and the Black Sea.Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov told Russian state news agency Tass that Kyiv was "resisting" Moscow's invasion but could not "change the current course of events."Meanwhile, in Ukraine, a woman was killed and a 6-year-old girl was among at least two other people wounded in two Russian attacks on the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia, local officials said Sunday.Russia continues energy attacks, Kyiv saysTrump announced on Oct. 11 that Russia and Ukraine had agreed to an "energy ceasefire" in the 4½-year-old war, but offered no details. Kyiv reported Russian attacks on energy sites continued after Trump's announcement, and on Thursday said it had resumed strikes on Russian oil facilities after a three-day pause.Zelenskyy wrote on X on Sunday that Russia had attacked Ukraine's energy, oil and gas sectors 76 times in the week since Trump's announcement. The Ukrainian government initially said it was observing the ceasefire.Also read: Trump's decision to waive Russian sanctions outrages Congress, but no quick counter seenEnergy facilities in four Ukrainian regions were struck overnight, leaving tens of thousands of families without power, he said, accusing Russia of trying to cause a blackout."America should see that Russia is not taking any reciprocal steps in response to sanctions relief or agreements. On the contrary, they take every signal of an opportunity to make money as proof that their bet on war is paying off and they can keep fighting," the Ukrainian president wrote.Ukraine apology to Lithuania over drone alertUkraine's Foreign Ministry apologized on Sunday after a drone entered Lithuania's airspace, prompting authorities to issue an air raid warning.Russian electronic warfare may have diverted the drone during a Ukrainian operation against legitimate military targets in Russia, ministry spokesperson Heorhii Tykhyi said in a statement.Lithuanian authorities urged residents in two northern counties along the Latvian border to take cover early Sunday because of a possible drone incursion, public broadcaster LRT reported.A drone entered the northern Pasvalys region and damaged a moving car, LRT said, citing Lithuania's National Crisis Management Center. No injuries were reported.

Mutual fund holdings of IT stocks sink to record low in September
items.summary: Mumbai: Indian mutual funds' exposure to Information Technology (IT) stocks fell to an all-time low in September as concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) disruption, weak global client spending and subdued growth prospects weighed on the sector. The decline has pushed frontline IT stocks such as Infosys and TCS, once among fund managers' biggest holdings, out of mutual funds' top holdings lists.IT stocks accounted for 5.3% of mutual funds' equity assets under management (AUM) in September, compared with 7.6% at the end of 2025 and 9.24% at the end of 2024. The sector's weight had touched a record 13.4% at the end of 2021."The correction in Information Technology stocks during 2026 has been a de-rating story more than an earnings story," said Harsh Thakkar, equity research analyst at Samco Securities.135037302The value of mutual funds' IT holdings fell 25% to ₹2.97 lakh crore in September from ₹3.98 lakh crore in December 2025, according to Prime Database. The value had reached a record ₹4.03 lakh crore in November 2025.Infosys, which was among the five largest holdings of mutual funds at the start of 2026, slipped to 10th place in September. TCS has seen a similar decline. The stock, which ranked 10th among mutual fund holdings in 2024 and was among the top 14 in 2025, slipped to 18th place in September.HCL Tech and Tech Mahindra, which ranked 20th and 25th among mutual funds' largest holdings at the beginning of 2026, slipped to 25th and 31st positions, respectively, in September. Wipro fell sharply to 316th place from 88th at the start of 2026 and 56th in 2024.Read more: Mega Jio Platforms IPO to lead Rs 31,663 crore offerings this week; 9 listings lined upMany fund managers have cut their exposure due to uncertainty over the extent of disruption that AI could bring into the software services industry."Revenue growth has remained muted but has not collapsed," said Thakkar. "However, valuations have fallen sharply because investors priced in the potential threat from AI agents to the labour-intensive application development and maintenance business model."Read more: Can Nifty, Sensex rally further or will bears reign in? 5 factors to steer market this weekWeighed down by these concerns, the Nifty IT index till October 8 had shed about 28% in 2026 as against the 14% decline in the Nifty. Exporters may have to track emissions
items.summary: New Delhi: The government has begun discussions on whether Indian exporters should track indirect emissions across their supply chains as trade partners tighten green requirements and global value chains become increasingly interconnected.The finance and commerce & industry ministries have held preliminary discussions on whether Scope 3 emissions should be measured for exports to all countries, rather than only for markets such as the European Union and the UK, which have introduced Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) measures.Scope 3 emissions cover indirect emissions across a company's value chain, including those linked to purchased goods and services, capital goods, transportation, waste, business travel, employee commuting, leased assets, raw material extraction and the sourcing of imported raw materials. Measuring them is more complex than tracking emissions directly generated by a company or those associated with the energy it purchases.Also Read | Faster services imports threaten to erode cushion against India’s goods trade deficit: Report"There is one thought that measurement of Scope 3 emissions can't be done for the EU alone. It would have to do for all countries because the value chains are linked," said an official, adding that the indirect nature of these emissions makes them particularly challenging to measure, report and mitigate. However, no decision has been taken on the issue.Niti Aayog, in its report titled Scenarios Towards Viksit Bharat And Net Zero: Financing Needs, has said that any inclusion of Scope 3 disclosures should be phased and proportionate, beginning with large entities in high-impact sectors to avoid imposing disproportionate compliance burdens on micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) and smaller suppliers.135034854The existing CBAM frameworks provide for the determination of direct and indirect greenhouse gas emissions covered under Scopes 1 and 2 of the Greenhouse Gas Protocol. Indian exporters of iron and steel, aluminium, cement, fertilisers, electricity and hydrogen products are already subject to the EU's CBAM.Also Read | What is holding up the US-India trade deal?"The CBAM is already a challenge for us because we don't have basic data on our raw material emissions. Disclosures on Scope 2 are posing a problem, so adding Scope 3 emissions data on what is my electricity provider and transportation would be unviable," said a steel exporter to the EU. Under the EU CBAM, the central platform will open for the sale of CBAM certificates on February 1, 2027. Importers must submit their first annual CBAM declaration and surrender certificates covering all 2026 imports by September 30, 2027.

items.title: Europe refused China, India oil sanctions
items.summary: Washington, Amid intense criticism, the US on Sunday said the waiver of sanctions on Russia and tariffs on other countries, including India, was a 60-day pause to analyse the global impact of the measure.Trump's cabinet colleagues Marco Rubio and Scott Bessent said the Lindsey O Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act granted the President the flexibility to assess the situation."No sanctions were lifted on Friday," Bessent told NBC's Meet the Press, referring to the Executive Order signed by Trump granting a waiver from sanctions under the Graham Act passed with overwhelming bipartisan support last month.Bessent revealed that the US had asked its European allies to impose secondary sanctions on China and India for buying Russian oil, but they refused."So why should the US bear the burden? President Trump, perhaps we will be in contact with our European partners. Why should the US go it alone," Bessent said, adding that European countries had waived an embargo on purchase of Russian diesel and jet fuel in May.On Saturday evening, Secretary of State Rubio said waivers were included in the Graham Act to study the different things going around the world, such as the pressure on global energy supplies due to the Iran war, the attack of Houthis in Saudi Arabia and the Ukraine-Russia war."I think the president wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyse what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy, and even to the US economy," Rubio told reporters before leaving on a six-day visit to Uzbekistan and India.The executive order signed by Trump on Friday states that the waivers shall remain in effect until such time as the President or the Secretary of State, in consultation with the Secretary of the Treasury and the Trade Representative, as appropriate, determine that further action is appropriate.Speaking to reporters at Mar-a-Lago resort near Miami on Saturday, Trump said his decision to waive sanctions under the Graham Act would benefit the US."A lot of you don't know what my decision is yet, but we'll figure it out, and you'll figure it out,"  he said."It's a very good decision, and it's going to be a decision that's good for the country, and I think good for the world because we're really at a world stage,"  Trump said.Bessent also accused the European nations of fuelling Russia's war on Ukraine by buying oil and gas from Moscow."The Europeans have given Russia and Vladimir Putin more money than they've given the Ukrainians. They continue to gorge on Russian energy," Bessent said."The Europeans are financing the Russian war machine. The US imports USD four billion of Russian products. USD 1.8 billion of that is fertiliser. The Europeans import more than 10 times that," Bessent said.Trump's decision to waive sanctions on Russia came under fire from the Republicans and Democrats, who last month came together to overwhelmingly pass the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act.Senator Darline Graham, a Republican from South Carolina, also criticised Trump for exempting Russia from a sanctions law that was championed by and named after her late brother Lindsey.Indian-American lawmakers, most of whom had voted against the Graham Act, were sharply critical of Trump's decision."Trump's decision to waive new sanctions on Russia should leave no doubt: that is exactly what is happening," Congressman Ami Bera said on X."My Republican colleagues pushed hard to pass the Lindsey Graham Russia sanctions bill before we left town. They ought to be standing up and screaming at the top of their lungs that we don't side with Russia," he said."Trump is doing exactly what we warned: undermining Congress' authority, abandoning Ukraine, and letting Putin off the hook," Congressman Suhas Subramanyam said on X."Republicans refused to let us vote on stronger Russia sanctions. Now we - and our allies - are paying the price," Subramanyam said.

It was also issues for western districts of Theni, Coimbatore and Nilgiris.Also Read: Southwest monsoon exits India with 13% rain deficitThe red alert means a forecast of extremely heavy rainfall above 20 cm, and the orange alert means a forecast of very heavy rainfall above 11 cm.The issued bulleting said Saturday's upper air cyclonic circulation over the northern part of the state and south coastal Andhra Pradesh had become less marked.Despite this, Chennai and its neighbouring districts saw their first and heavy spell of rains. The weather report mentioned that Parry's Corner in Chennai received the highest rainfall. This was followed by Kathivakkam.The Greater Chennai Corporation said that pro-active field operations, constant rescue efforts and continued coordination made sure that major areas and subways did not face waterlogging amid severe weather conditions.A team from the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and four teams from the Tamil Nadu Disaster Response Force (TNDRF) were deployed on the ground to handle vulnerable areas. Nine relief centres were established, and food was being steadily distributed to residents.Also Read: India faces weakest monsoon in nearly two decades as El Nino strengthensRainwater has now been completely cleared from all major bus routes and streets. Pumping operations in remaining low-lying pockets were in final stages and would end shortly, thereby keeping the entire situation under control.Chief Minister C Joseph Vijay and Minister for Public Works and Youth Welfare and Sports Development, Aadhav Arjuna, visited the Ripon Building, GCC headquarters, following heavy rainfall across the city and red alert.During his visit, Aadhav Arjuna met teams from NDRF and TNDRF deployed for rescue operations, held consultations, and issued necessary directives regarding rescue and relief measures.

items.summary: In a historic step, the Central Industrial Security Force (CISF) will implement a major functional reorganisation of its administrative and operational structure from November 1 to strengthen specialised security management across critical infrastructure and strategic establishments nationwide.The reorganisation, approved by the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA), will realign the force's existing territorial sectors according to the specific security requirements of different industries and establishments, including power, coal, steel, petroleum and natural gas, ports, government buildings, museums, monuments and mass rapid transit systems.Under the revised structure, the force said, the National Capital Region Sector will be reorganised as the Government Building Museums and Monuments and Mass Rapid Transit System (GBMM & MRTS) Sector, New Delhi.The North Sector in New Delhi and North Eastern Sector-II in Kolkata will be restructured as the Power-I and Power-II Sectors, respectively. The Eastern Sector in Ranchi will become the Coal Sector, while the Central Sector in Bhilai will be converted into the Steel Sector.Similarly, the North Eastern Sector in Guwahati will become the Petroleum and Natural Gas Sector. The Western Sector in Mumbai and the South Sector in Chennai will be transformed into the West Coast Port Sector and East Coast Port Sector, respectively.The existing Department of Atomic Energy and Department of Space (DAE & DoS) Sector in Bengaluru, Airport Sector-I in New Delhi and Airport Sector-II in Bengaluru will continue under their respective functional arrangements.The reorganisation, it said, aims to improve operational oversight, develop sector-specific expertise, ensure greater uniformity in security practices and strengthen coordination with the concerned ministries, departments and installation managements.The CISF provides security to a wide range of establishments, including airports, seaports, atomic energy and space installations, power plants, power grids, steel plants, coal mines, petroleum and natural gas facilities, currency note presses, government buildings, iconic monuments and mass transit systems.Each sector has distinct operational processes, infrastructure, potential hazards and security vulnerabilities, requiring specialised security arrangements.Under the earlier system, administrative and operational supervision was largely organised on the basis of territorial jurisdiction. Over the past 25 years, the force has progressively adopted a functional approach in selected sectors, including aviation and strategic establishments under the Department of Atomic Energy and the Department of Space.The experience gained from this approach highlighted the advantages of specialised supervision, focused training, sector-specific Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs), better utilisation of specialised personnel and closer coordination with the concerned organisations.Building on this experience, the CISF reviewed the supervisory structure of the remaining territorial sectors and undertook the functional realignment following deliberations with supervisory formations, branches at force headquarters and senior officers, before obtaining MHA approval.The restructuring assumes significance as the CISF's mandate is expanding beyond conventional industrial security to cover new and specialised responsibilities.The force has been designated as a Recognised Security Organisation (RSO) for port facilities under the International Ship and Port Facility Security (ISPS) Code. The functional realignment of port-sector supervision is expected to support specialised port-security expertise and improve coordination with port authorities and other stakeholders.The CISF has also been entrusted with security responsibilities at high-security correctional facilities in Jammu and Kashmir and designated as the nodal agency for aerial security of critical infrastructure.The force is strengthening its cybersecurity and drone and anti-drone capabilities through specialised training and collaboration with premier institutions to improve preparedness against cyberattacks, digital threats and hostile unmanned aerial systems.The reorganisation is expected to establish a more specialised, sector-oriented security apparatus, improve operational accountability and strengthen protection of India's strategic and economic assets.

Instead of changing the court-fee system, the rules focus on administrative enforcement, accountability and time-bound conflict resolution.

items.title: Poor management, workplace culture key reasons behind job switch: Report
items.summary:
Career decisions are not driven by salary alone; rather, factors like poor management or workplace culture also play a key role for employees considering a job change, a report said on Sunday.
End-to-end workforce staffing and HR solutions provider Genius HRTech Limited's September 2026 report revealed that 47 per cent of respondents cited poor management or workplace culture as a key reason for considering a job change, while 30 per cent pointed to compensation below market expectations.
The Genius HRTech report is based on inputs from 1,255 employees during September 1-30 across sectors, including Information Technology (IT), manufacturing, telecom, retail, finance and BFSI, FMCG and engineering, among others.
Further, the report found that 39 per cent of respondents would be more likely to stay with their current employer if offered better management, a healthier workplace culture or greater flexibility.

items.title: Trivandrum airport halts flights on Tue
items.summary: Flight operations at Thiruvananthapuram International Airport will be suspended for five hours on October 20 to allow the traditional Arattu procession of Sree Padmanabhaswamy Temple to pass across the runway.Thiruvananthapuram International Airport Ltd (TIAL) said on Sunday that flight services would remain suspended from 4 pm to 9 pm to facilitate the temple’s ‘Alpassi Arattu’ procession. Passengers have been advised to check revised flight timings with their respective airlines.Also read: Vietnam Airlines set to fly non-stop between Hanoi and Ahmedabad from November 2026The temporary suspension is part of a centuries-old tradition associated with the Travancore royal family. The procession takes the ceremonial idols of the temple to Shangumugham beach for a ritual holy bath before returning to the shrine.The airport has adjusted its operations twice a year for decades to accommodate the temple’s biannual Arattu processions. The practice continues despite the growth of the airport and changes in its management.The tradition dates back to the period of the erstwhile Travancore kingdom and has continued since the airport was established in 1932.Also read: Indian passport rises to 84th rank in Henley Passport Index 2026; visa-free access to 55 destinationsAccording to historians, the then Travancore king, Sree Chithira Thirunal, had stipulated that the airport would remain open to the public for 363 days a year, with the remaining two days reserved for Lord Padmanabha, the titular deity of the royal family.The ritual has continued even after the Adani Group took over the airport’s management. The runway crossing is a distinctive feature of the ceremony, reflecting the historical relationship between the temple, the former royal family and the airport. The temporary closure requires airlines to adjust their schedules to accommodate the procession.Passengers travelling to or from Thiruvananthapuram on October 20 should check with their airlines for updated departure and arrival times before heading to the airport.

The restriction, initially imposed on April 23, 2025, has been extended periodically since then amid strained relations between the two neighbouring countries.
The Pakistan Airports Authority (PAA) announced the extension in a post on X on Saturday, saying the restriction also covers military flights.
The latest extension will remain in effect until 4:59 am (local time) on November 24, 2026, according to the authority.
A PAA spokesperson said a fresh Notice to Airmen (NOTAM) had been issued to extend the ban, Geo News reported.
Pakistan's airspace is divided into two flight information regions (FIRs) -- Karachi and Lahore, according to a Pakistan Civil Aviation Authority (PCAA) document from 2022. The latest NOTAM applies to both the Karachi and Lahore FIRs.

"This literally is the first time I've heard of this," Vance said in response.

items.title: Tata Trusts disbursed ₹1,556 crore in FY26, plans 40-50 nonprofit hospitals
items.summary:
Tata Trusts, India's largest philanthropic group, disbursed Rs 1,556.31 crore in the year to March 2026 and is now working toward a network of 40 to 50 not-for-profit general hospitals, Chairman Noel Tata said in the Trusts' Annual Report for 2025-26.
Tata said patients who can afford to pay would help fund care for those who cannot. The report gives no investment figure, locations, or timeline for the hospitals.
In his message, Tata said the Trusts want to build institutions and models that become "enduring public assets" and be judged on what changes as a result of their work. He wrote that measuring philanthropy by people reached or money spent is no longer enough.
Institutional grants and direct project spending came in at Rs 1,353.32 crore, and individual grants at  Rs 202.99 crore. Rural upliftment took the largest share at Rs 457.62 crore, followed by education (Rs 270.26 crore), cancer care (Rs 178.46 crore), institutions (Rs 169.31 crore) and healthcare (Rs 105.97 crore). .

"A lot of you don't know what my decision is yet, but we'll figure it out, and you'll figure it out," Trump told reporters at the Mar-a-Lago resort in Miami on Saturday evening.
"It's a very good decision, and it's going to be a decision that's good for the country, and I think good for the world because we're really at a world stage," Trump said.

Overall production is estimated to decline by 2.11 per cent from the previous season, the association said.

Japan is set to launch a spacecraft on the world's first mission to bring back samples from Phobos, one of the two small, potato-shaped moons orbiting Mars.
Scientists hope the mission, which is expected to take five years, will provide clues to how Phobos and its smaller sibling Deimos formed, and hopefully even shed light on the origins of life in the solar system.
The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency's launch of the spacecraft Tuesday on a new Japanese mainstay H-3 rocket comes as the United States, China and others consider sending astronauts to Mars.
Samples from Phobos will provide useful data for scientists to consider using a Martian moon as a base for a future manned mission to the planet, said MMX project manager Yasuhiro Kawakatsu.
"Despite their potential importance, Martian moons have never been fully investigated," Kawakatsu said. "They are known as the most important unclimbed mountains in the solar system."

items.summary:
US President Donald Trump wants to take a 60-day period to analyse what imposing sanctions on Russia and tariffs on other countries would mean for the global economy, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said here.
Rubio was responding to questions on Saturday evening ahead of his departure for a week-long tour of Uzbekistan and India.
"I think the president wants to take the 60-day period of time to sort of analyse what imposing both sanctions and tariffs will mean to the global economy, and even to the US economy," Rubio said in response to a question on the waivers granted by Trump under the Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act or the Graham Act.
On Friday, Trump waived key provisions of the Graham Act that authorised punitive tariffs on countries purchasing Russian oil, offering relief to India.

items.summary:
Rioters clashed with police, looted stores and set property on fire in central Milan on Saturday, emptying Piazza del Duomo and a luxury shopping arcade when the area would usually be teeming with shoppers.
The march against wars and rising living costs began peacefully. But masked protesters threw stones, paving blocks and other objects at riot police and set fire to barricades made from bar tables. Images of the aftermath showed a severely damaged carabinieri car.
Police used water cannons and tear gas to disperse the crowds.
At least two police officers were injured and about 50 demonstrators, including many minors, were detained, the LaPresse news agency reported.
Italian Premier Giorgia Meloni condemned the violence in a social media post.
"Demonstrating is a right. Setting our cities ablaze is not," she wrote, citing "hooligans who exploit demonstrations to sow chaos, attack those responsible for ensuring security and hold entire cities hostage".

Warrants executed. Subpoenas issued. American first. items.title: US to revive 3 shuttered nuclear plants to meet rising electricity demand
items.summary:
The United States is making an unprecedented attempt to revive three shuttered nuclear plants to meet rising energy demand, including from large-scale data centres.
No commercial nuclear reactor is known to have resumed generating electricity after beginning the decommissioning process that takes one out of service, though some reactors have restarted after long outages.
The Department of Energy is lending as much as USD 4.4 billion to restart the Palisades Power Plant in Michigan, the Crane Clean Energy Centre on Pennsylvania's Three Mile Island and the Duane Arnold Energy Centre in Iowa to restore a combined 2.25 gigawatts of electricity, which can power roughly 2 million homes and businesses. All three of the plants closed before their licenses expired, largely because the electricity they produced was considered too expensive.
Not anymore. Two of the plants have contracts with Big Tech companies that will pay a premium to get large amounts of carbon-free energy for data centres.

A security official and a traffic controller said an area of the Aden airport that hosts a military unit aligned with the Saudi-backed government was hit. Both spoke on condition of anonymity because they were not authorized to speak to the media.

While Dipke was picked up from his home in Jhandewalan, Bohra was detained in Mandi House, both in Central Delhi. There was chaos with jostling crowds, camera crews and swarms of security personnel as the two were detained.

items.title: PNGRB clears IGX platform to book unused LNG regasification capacity
items.summary:
Oil and gas regulator PNGRB has approved a proposal by the Indian Gas Exchange (IGX) to introduce a platform for listing and booking unutilised liquefied natural gas (LNG) regasification capacity, in a move aimed at improving infrastructure utilisation and widening access to the country's gas market.
The Petroleum and Natural Gas Regulatory Board (PNGRB) said the voluntary platform would allow LNG terminal operators and capacity holders to list unused capacity, enabling prospective users to identify and book available slots according to their requirements.
The initiative comes as several LNG terminals report low capacity utilisation, leaving scope to attract additional cargoes by offering unused regasification capacity at competitive charges. Regasification is the process of converting LNG, transported in liquid form, back into gas for supply through pipelines.

items.summary:
The poll officials have started reverification of more than 47 lakh voters whose names were removed from the draft electoral rolls, to ensure that no eligible voter is left out in the ongoing special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, Chief Electoral Officer (CEO) Ashok Kumar said on Friday.
The development comes amid complaints that the names of many living voters and those who were living at their registered address were also removed from the draft rolls published on August 31.
Kumar said that around 25 lakh cases out of 33.12 lakh, in which voters who were issued notices for non-mapping or logical discrepancy, have also been resolved.
Speaking with reporters, Kumar said, "The booth-level officers have been directed to reverify the voters whose names were not in the draft rolls published after the enumeration phase. Our efforts are to ensure that no genuine voter's name is omitted in the final voters lists that will be published on December 4."

Out-of-favour Indian women's cricket team top-order batter Punam Raut on Thursday announced her retirement from all forms of international cricket with immediate effect.
The 37-year-old Raut has played four Tests, 73 ODIs and 35 T20Is for India between 2009 and 2021.
"After much thought and reflection, I have decided to retire from international cricket in all formats of the game," Raut said in a post on her Instagram page.
"Representing India has been the greatest honour of my life. Cricket has been more than just a sport - it has shaped my character, taught me resilience, and given me memories that I will cherish forever. Every time I wore the India jersey, I did so with immense pride and gratitude.
"Wearing the India jersey was a dream that became a reality, and I will always be grateful for the trust and support I received."
Raut also credited her domestic team for shaping her career.

items.title: Tennis player Stefan Milicevic handed 24-year suspension for match-fixing
items.summary:
- Serbian tennis player Stefan Milicevic has been given a 24-year ban for allegedly fixing multiple matches and recruiting other players into a "corrupt network," the International Tennis Integrity Agency said Thursday.
The agency said the 29-year-old Milicevic was charged with fixing six matches - including five of his own - and trying to fix six more between 2022 and 2024. He is banned from tennis until 2050.
Milicevic never reached a singles ranking higher than 1,338 and only played in lower-tier events. But the ITIA also charged him with recruiting "multiple professional players as part of a corrupt network" that resulted in "a number of other players fixing matches" during those same years.
The agency did not give details about which matches were fixed, or name any of the other players involved.
It said Milicevic did not cooperate into its investigation into the fixed matches and did not respond to its findings. It also fined Milicevic $70,000.

items.title: Fed Chair Warsh stresses price stability, offers no signals on rate outlook
items.summary:
Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh said Friday he won't prejudge what the US central bank will do about interest rates at its upcoming meetings in October and December.
The Fed increased its key interest rate by a quarter-point to about 3.9 per cent in September, its first increase in three years, and stubbornly elevated US inflation will likely lead it to hike that rate again in coming months to slow spending and help cool price pressures.
But Warsh offered no fresh signals during a "fireside chat" with International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva at a meeting of financial leaders in Bangkok.
"At the Federal Reserve, we made very clear that we would deliver price stability, and we removed a dose of accommodation about a month ago," Warsh said. "I don't prejudge meetings. I don't believe in saying now what I might do at the meetings that we have in the balance of this year."

items.title: Air India extends cancellation of Saudi Arabia flights till October 20
items.summary:
Air India on Friday said it has extended the cancellation of flights to Saudi Arabia till October 20 amid escalating tensions in the region due to the attacks on the Gulf country by Houthis.
Earlier, the airline as well as Air India Express had cancelled flights to Saudi Arabia till October 17.
"In view of the evolving situation in Saudi Arabia, all Air India flights to and from Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah stand cancelled until 20 October 2026," Air India said in a post on X.
The airline also said it was closely monitoring developments and continuously assessing the situation to ensure the safe resumption of operations.
"Passengers affected by these cancellations are being offered a full refund," it added.
IndiGo, on Thursday, announced extending the cancellation of flights to Saudi Arabia till October 24.
On Thursday, Akasa Air said that in view of the prevailing security situation in the Middle East, it has extended the suspension of all flights to and from Riyadh until October 2

items.summary: The youth-led Cockroach Janata Party is expected to hold a march with the Indian tri-colour in Connaught Place's Central Park on Friday, with authorities in the national capital set to restrict a planned demonstration.CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke has called on supporters to gather in Central Delhi for the rally at 5 PM, while 220 companies of Central Armed Police Forces and an expanded CCTV camera network have been put into service in the area. The central part of the capital remained heavily guarded in the early hours of Friday.The call for the rally comes after two leaders of the Gen-Z led outfit, Sourav Das and Ashutosh Ranka were sent to judicial custody for five days after removing barricades and entering Jantar Mantar, which was recently de-notified as a protest side. Amnesty International India has called for the immediate release of both Ranka and Das, saying both the arrests and removal of Jantar Mantar as a protest site threatens right to dissent.The confrontation sets up another test of how authorities handle the protests, following last weekend’s detention of thousands and an effective lockdown of parts of the capital. Officials said Central Park, the planned venue for Friday’s demonstration, would remain closed for two days.

A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi declined to entertain the plea and said, "We hope better sense will prevail on everyone. Small shopkeepers earn their livelihood during these days. We know the hardship and difficulty entire families will face."
Justice Bagchi observed that the various issues surrounding the protest, including the right to protest, the proposed selling of 'mungfali' and concerns over law and order, were interconnected.
"Someone wants to protest, someone wants to sell 'mungfali', someone wants law and order. All these are related," Justice Bagchi said.

items.title: India GDP to grow 7.1-7.3% in FY27 on private investment revival: Deloitte
items.summary:
The Indian economy is expected to grow by 7.1-7.3 per cent in the current fiscal, with a sustained revival in private investment providing an additional source of demand, Deloitte India said on Friday.
However, geopolitical tensions, volatile energy prices and trade disruptions pose risks to the growth outlook, it added.
Deloitte India Economist Rumki Majumdar said over the past decade, India's growth has rested on resilient household spending and sustained investment push in public infrastructure. Businesses now have better connectivity, healthier balance sheets, and higher capacity utilisation, which strengthens the case for expansion.
"The question is whether these conditions will encourage private investment to play a larger role in boosting growth in the coming years. Recent indicators offer grounds for optimism. Gross fixed capital formation grew by 11.9 per cent in the first quarter of FY 2026-27, its fastest expansion in four years," Majumdar said.

The attacker, identified as a Bend resident, forced his way into the school by shooting at locked doors, police said. He was shot and went down inside the school shortly after officers arrived, police spokesperson Sheila Miller said.

items.title: Indian rice cooks up a 1-year price high
items.summary: Asian rice export prices in key hubs remained firm this week, with Indian rates hitting a more than one-year high on stronger rupee and crop supply concerns, while Vietnamese prices rose to a near two-month high on expectations of stronger demand.India's 5% broken parboiled variety  was quoted at $384-$389 per ton this week, up from last week's $378-$384. Indian 5% broken white rice was priced at $385 to $390 per ton."Paddy prices remain firm in the domestic market due to limited supplies. Production has declined in several states because of below-normal rainfall," said a Mumbai-based exporter.Vietnam's 5% broken rice  was offered at $440-$450 per metric ton on Thursday, its highest level since August 21, up from $420-$430 a week ago."We are told that the Philippines will resume rice purchases from Vietnam from November," a trader based in Ho Chi Minh City said.A Vietnamese agriculture ministry official said this week that rice export activity is expected to be busy during the rest of this year, adding that the country's target to export 8 million tons of rice will be met.In Thailand, 5% broken rice  was quoted at $480 per ton, highest since September 10, up from $465 to $468 last week.The arrival of vessels to collect rice shipments and additional purchases by some exporters pushed prices higher, a Bangkok-based rice trader said.Flooding has delayed loading, while some exporters have had to buy additional rice as the off-season harvest nears its end, adding upward pressure on prices, the trader said.Thailand's rice exports could fall short of this year's 7-million-ton target amid competition from India and Pakistan and weaker demand from major buyers, according to the Thai Rice Exporters Association.In Bangladesh, rice prices rose over the past week, driven by higher fuel costs and rising paddy prices, with fine rice rising to 74-75 taka per kilogram from 72 taka a week earlier, adding to the financial strain on consumers already grappling with persistently high living costs.($1 = 122.4000 taka)

items.summary: A US federal judge has ordered the Trump administration to reopen registration for the 2027 Diversity Visa lottery, also known as the Green Card lottery, with the entry window set to open by November 1, 2026.The ruling restores a route to US permanent residency for eligible applicants after the government failed to start registration on time, according to Courthouse News Service report.Also Read: US judge blocks Trump policy of fining migrants up to $1.8 millionUS District Judge Jinsook Ohta issued the order on October 14, directing Secretary of State Marco Rubio and the US State Department to announce the registration dates and open the entry process for 30 days.The State Department must also accept eligible entries, notify selected applicants and process their cases under the programme's rules, the report said. A subsequent extension moved the registration deadline to November 1 and the deadline to notify selected applicants to December 3.Also Read: US raises select immigration fees for FY 2027, new charges from October 16Earlier in November 2025, the State Department had announced that it was making changes to the entry process for the 2027 lottery and would announce the registration dates later. The registration delay prompted California-based immigration law firm Red Eagle Law to file a lawsuit against the State Department. The firm argued that the government's failure to open registration had effectively cancelled the annual programme.The Diversity Visa programme offers up to 55,000 immigrant visas each year to eligible applicants from countries with historically low rates of immigration to the US.Applicants selected through the lottery must also meet eligibility requirements and complete the visa process as the selection in itself does not guarantee a Green Card.The 2027 programme's visa year ends on September 30, 2027. items.title: US proposes ending H-1B deference policy
items.summary: The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has proposed ending a policy that generally allows immigration officers to rely on earlier approvals when reviewing certain visa extensions. The change could lead to fresh scrutiny of H-1B petitions, more document requests and higher costs for employers.What is the proposed change?The proposal would remove a rule that asks US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) officers to generally respect earlier eligibility decisions when the same parties and facts remain unchanged.Also Read: US ends 540-day automatic work permit extension for immigrants: What changes nowUnder the current policy, officers generally rely on an earlier approval when considering an extension if the circumstances remain the same. They can depart from that decision if they find a significant error, a major change in circumstances or new information that affects eligibility.If the proposal takes effect, officers could reassess each extension request even when the circumstances have not changed. Employers would need to establish that workers continue to meet the requirements for their visa category.Why could H-1B workers be affected?H-1B workers seeking to extend their stay in the US could face closer scrutiny of their petitions. Employers may have to provide additional documents to establish that their employees remain eligible.Also Read: Bahrain’s 90-day temporary work rule explained: What Indian expats need to knowDHS said the existing policy could limit officers' ability to examine cases fully and identify errors or possible fraud. The department said removing the requirement would strengthen checks and ensure employers continue to prove that their workers qualify for the requested immigration benefit.The change could affect H-1B workers from India and other countries, as well as their employers, by subjecting extension petitions to fresh scrutiny. Workers could face additional document requests and delays if USCIS seeks further evidence to verify their eligibility.More paperwork and costs for employersDHS estimates that the change could lead to 6,044 additional requests for evidence (RFEs) each year and cost petitioners about $133,987 annually.An RFE is a notice from USCIS asking an employer or applicant to provide more documents or information before the agency decides a case. Responding to such a notice can increase the time and work involved in an application.The department also warned that more detailed reviews could lengthen processing times and create uncertainty for workers seeking to continue their employment in the US. Additional reviews could increase USCIS's workload and put pressure on its processing resources.The proposed change applies to Form I-129, which employers use to petition for non-immigrant workers. The form covers H-1B petitions as well as several other worker visa categories.The proposal is not a final rule and has not taken effect. DHS is accepting public comments until November 13, 2026, and will consider the feedback before making a final decision.

items.summary: RIYADH, - The Saudi-led military coalition in Yemen said on Thursday that the country's Houthis had attempted to attack dozens of Saudi airports, ports and oil facilities, as fighting between the Iran-aligned group and Saudi Arabia intensified.The Houthis have been firing ballistic missiles and drones at key Saudi sites for a week, in response to the kingdom's backing of government forces in Yemen's renewed civil war. The coalition's latest statement highlighted the risk to Saudi civilian infrastructure as the conflict escalated.Coalition spokesperson Turki al-Maliki said at a press conference that the Houthis had launched 20 attacks on King Khalid International Airport in Riyadh this month, killing 17 people and wounding 333 others. The airport, one of Saudi Arabia's main international aviation hubs, was among the civilian infrastructure targeted in what the coalition described as a series of attacks.The coalition also said Houthi attacks on Abha airport, in southwestern Saudi Arabia near the Yemeni border, had killed three people and wounded 28.Maliki said the Houthis had acquired advanced military technology with the help of "regional actors," including ballistic missiles, drones and explosive-laden fast boats.The spokesperson also said the coalition had destroyed 127 weapons storage facilities and launch platforms in Yemen's mountainous areas.He called on the Houthis to immediately halt operations targeting civilians and civilian infrastructure, and said the group should read the coalition's statement carefully and "between the lines."Shortly after the coalition's statement, the Houthi military spokesperson said Saudi airspace and airports were unsafe, renewing a warning to airlines while excluding airspace over the holy cities of Mecca and Medina.Yemen has been mired in conflict since the Houthis seized the capital Sanaa in 2014, prompting a Saudi-led military intervention the following year. The UN-brokered truce in 2022 largely halted major fighting, and a de facto truce held even after it expired six months later. But efforts to turn it into a lasting political settlement have stalled as regional tensions have intensified.

items.title: Musk now wants to make an Amazon rival
items.summary: Tesla and SpaceX founder Elon Musk wants to start a competitor to Amazon. The billionaire made the statement on X, the social media platform he owns.Musk's statement came in response to an X user who complained that Amazon was blocking Grok bots from placing orders."Amazon is blocking Grok @bots from ordering, and Elon's answer is just have your bot buy it somewhere else. One of my Grok bots only handles my Amazon returns, so I'm watching this one closely," said an X user who goes by the name Nick.Responding to the complaint, Musk wrote, "Maybe we should start a competitor to Amazon."It is unclear whether Musk was joking or seriously considering the idea.Nick responded, "I would sign up in a heartbeat !! Fast delivery should be included in your X subscription."Another X user suggested the name "xshop", while a third suggested that Musk should simply buy Amazon.Musk is the world's richest person, with a net worth of more than $900 billion, while Amazon founder Jeff Bezos follows him with a fortune of around $370 billion.Musk-Bezos rivalryElon Musk and Jeff Bezos have been rivals for years, with their differences often playing out in public. According to Business Insider, their rivalry dates back to a reportedly contentious dinner in 2004. Both billionaires have since competed in the space industry, with Musk leading SpaceX and Bezos founding Blue Origin.In 2013, the two clashed over access to a NASA launchpad and patents related to rocket landings. Two years later, Musk took a dig at Bezos on Twitter over rocket-landing technology, arguing that Blue Origin was years behind SpaceX.Their exchanges have extended beyond space exploration. In 2021, Musk responded to a Washington Post reporter seeking comment for a story about him by saying, "Give my regards to your puppet master."Bezos, meanwhile, has questioned the feasibility of colonising Mars, a central ambition of SpaceX. Speaking to SpaceNews in 2019, he said, "My friends who want to move to Mars, I say, do me a favor and go live on the top of Mount Everest for a year first, and see if you like it, because it’s a garden paradise compared to Mars."

items.title: Current account deficit narrows to $5.2 billion in August: RBI data
items.summary:
India's current account deficit narrowed to USD 5.2 billion in August from USD 6.1 billion a year ago, aided by a lower merchandise trade deficit and higher surpluses in services trade, according to preliminary data released by the RBI on Thursday.
The net deficit in the merchandise trade account declined to USD 26.6 billion in August from USD 27.6 billion in the same month last year.
Merchandise exports rose to USD 44.7 billion in August from USD 35.1 billion a year ago, while imports increased to USD 71.3 billion from USD 62.7 billion, the RBI data showed.
The surplus in services trade increased to USD 16.5 billion in August from USD 15.6 billion a year ago. Services exports rose to USD 35.5 billion from USD 31.2 billion, while imports increased to USD 18.9 billion from USD 15.6 billion.
Net transfers, including remittances, increased to USD 12.8 billion in August from USD 12.2 billion a year ago, while the net deficit in the income account widened to USD 8 billion from USD 6.3 .

items.title: Reliance Jio’s next big bet is beyond data
items.summary: IPO-bound Reliance Jio is looking to go beyond data connectivity by partnering with technology companies to create new markets, rather than simply distribute their products, Akash Ambani revealed on Thursday, citing the telecom operator’s collaboration with Google on its artificial intelligence service Gemini.“This is not a simple distribution deal,” Ambani, Jio platforms' Managing Director, said at Jio’s IPO press conference, explaining how the partnership had helped create a market for Google’s flagship AI product in India.Also read: Jio IPO: With tech muscle, Akash Ambani makes $1.4 tn digital economy pitchGoogle already has a significant presence in India, with more than a billion users across each of its platforms, and Gemini as its flagship product. Yet the company partnered with Jio, Ambani said, drawing a parallel with how the telecom operator had approached the data market.“What we were able to do, like we did with the data market, was co-create a new market,” he said.The partnership has since resulted in Gemini adding 13 million new subscribers to its paid service, Ambani said, pointing to the opportunity Jio sees in working with technology companies beyond conventional connectivity.Jio eyes share of $1.4 trillion digital economyAmbani said Jio Platforms aims to capture a significant share of India's projected $1.4 trillion digital economy by FY31, citing its technology capabilities and end-to-end technology stack."We see $1.4 trillion digital economy by FY31. The end-to-end stack gives us the ability to capture a large market share for this," he said.The technology-led growth strategy is central to Jio's pitch to investors ahead of its public listing, as the company looks to expand digital services, technology platforms and enterprise businesses alongside its telecom operations.Ambani said Jio had filed 7,200 patents so far, placing it among the world's leading companies in patent filings. "We are the only Indian company among top 20 global companies in terms of patents filed. 7200 patents filed till now for Jio," he said.5G network and global partnershipsAmbani also pointed to Jio's network reach and pricing as advantages in expanding access to digital services across India."Mission of Jio is connect every Indian home to highest order of digital services. We are the largest 5G base outside China. Our pricing per GB is the lowest anywhere in the world," he said.Jio has expanded beyond mobile connectivity into home broadband, entertainment, cloud services, enterprise technology and artificial intelligence. Its subscriber base stood at about 533 million at the end of June 2026, providing a potential customer base for additional digital offerings."Some of the biggest global tech companies like Google have partnered with us," Ambani said. Google holds a 7.73% stake in Jio Platforms, while Meta owns about 9.98%. Both were among the investors that backed the company during its 2020 fundraising exercise.Also read: Marine Drive was lit up for Reliance IPO: Uday Kotak recalls Dhirubhai Ambani’s legacyJio IPO: Price band, issue size and datesJio Platforms has set a price band of Rs 1,065-1,119 per share for its IPO, which opens on October 21 and closes on October 23. The anchor investor book opens on October 19, with listing expected on October 28.The company plans to issue up to 27 crore fresh equity shares, raising as much as Rs 30,213 crore at the upper end of the price band. At that price, the offering values Jio Platforms at about Rs 10.3 lakh crore, or roughly $108 billion.The IPO could surpass Hyundai Motor India's Rs 27,900 crore issue in 2024 to become India's largest public offering. It will comprise an entirely fresh issue, with no offer for sale by existing shareholders.Jio has also reserved shares worth up to Rs 2,500 crore for eligible Reliance Industries shareholders and Rs 500 crore for eligible employees. Retail investors can apply for a minimum of 12 shares, requiring Rs 13,428 at the upper end of the price band.

items.title: India's trade gap widens to $30.21 bn in Sep
items.summary: India's merchandise trade deficit widened to $30.21 billion in September from $26.86 billion in August as imports grew faster than exports, government data released on Thursday showed, amid rising oil prices and supply disruptions linked to the escalating US-Iran conflict.The deficit was broadly in line with economists' expectations of $30.4 billion, according to a Reuters poll.Merchandise imports rose to $74.61 billion in September from $70.67 billion in the previous month, while exports increased marginally to $44.40 billion from $43.81 billion.The widening trade gap comes as the conflict involving the United States and Iran continues to disrupt global energy supplies, raising inflation concerns for India, the world's third-largest oil importer.Brent crude futures have remained above $100 per barrel amid the conflict, while attacks around the Strait of Hormuz have intensified over the past 10 days. Iran has said it is escalating strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions imposed last month.Also Read: India's trade deficit with China crosses USD 100 bn in first 9-monthsAgainst this backdrop, the Reserve Bank of India raised interest rates earlier this month to contain inflationary pressures and subsequently announced measures to support the rupee.Despite the widening deficit, export growth remained broad-based across several sectors.Trade Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said the increase reflected "India's strength across sectors including petroleum products, meat, dairy, poultry, electronic goods, handicrafts, and engineering goods."India is also seeking to diversify its export destinations, with its trade agreement with New Zealand scheduled to take effect next week, its pact with Britain already operational and a broader agreement with the European Union moving towards implementation.Automobile exports provided some support, rising 22.5% year-on-year to 684,481 vehicles in September 2026, according to separate data released by the Society of Indian Automobile Manufacturers (SIAM).Two-wheeler exports led the increase, jumping 26.8% to 544,797 units, although passenger vehicle shipments declined 2.2%.Meanwhile, services exports were estimated at $36.35 billion in September, compared with imports of $19.44 billion, according to trade ministry figures.Gold imports declined to $1.8 billion from $2.3 billion in August, when purchases had increased due to inventory restocking ahead of the festive season.During the first six months of FY27, gold imports fell 27.32% year-on-year to $19.27 billion.The United States remained India's largest export destination, with merchandise shipments rising to $50.81 billion during April-September from $45.82 billion in the corresponding period last year.

However, ongoing external macroeconomic pressures are likely to temper further gains, they said.
At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 94.95, then gained ground to touch 94.86, registering a gain of 31 paise over its previous close.
On Wednesday, the rupee appreciated 19 paise to close at 95.17 against the US dollar.
The rupee has now crossed 95.5095.00 range, bringing 94.80 into focus, CR Forex Advisors MD Amit Pabari said.
"A sustained break below 94.80 could open the door to another 5075 paise of appreciation. And the reduced direct dollar demand from oil companies could support the momentum," Pabari .

items.title: SIR storm reaches the Supreme Court
items.summary: The Supreme Court issued a notice to the Election Commission of India over the plea by Rahul Gandhi and other opposition members over mass voter deletions and alleged irregularities in the revision of voter rolls exercise.The country's top court is seeking response from the Election Commission of India, Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi on Gandhi and others' plea.Also Read: SC likely to hear Rahul Gandhi, INDIA bloc leader’s plea against ECI’s SIR decisions tomorrowIt is hearing a plea on which challenges India's controversial revision in voter roles, as the opposition bloc looks to suspend the exercise and hold the top election official accountable after series of mass protests and detentions.The apex court is also hearing multiple petitions pertaining to detention of protestors by the Delhi Police, alleged brutality and multiple restrictions of free travel and movement in the national capital. It will also be scrutinising the detention of multiple Supreme Court lawyers and journalists, along with a curb on internet usage in cenral Delhi over the last weekend.SC's notice to Election Commission over RaGa's pleaThe top court issued notice on a petition filed by Gandhi and nine other INDIA bloc leaders challenging the revision of electoral rolls.A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi remarked while issuing notice, “We would also ask one of the petitioners about his conduct.” The bench sought response from ECI, CEC Gyanesh Kumar, Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi on Gandhi and others' plea.The petition follows an Opposition march towards the Supreme Court on October 12, led by Gandhi, against the SIR exercise.A quick background checkThe expected hearing comes on the heels of massive protests led by India's opposition political parties and youth-led outfit Cockroach Janata Party after a report by the Indian Express alleged Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar authorised decisions without the consent of other Election Commissioners and disregarded their objections regarding the Special Intensive Revision of Electoral Rolls.The SIR exercise, launched in 2025, has led to more than 13 crore names being removed from draft voter lists. Opposition parties have alleged that eligible voters are being left out to aide the interests of the ruling BJP.The Election Commission and the BJP have defended the SIR exercise saying that the move is to ensure voter rolls remain transparent and not have names of deceased, duplicate or inelligible voters. The Opposition has called for the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar and for independent probes into the working of the poll body. The BJP has criticised the opposition parties, saying they have lost elections due to poor leadership and rejection from voters rather than due to the SIR process.India is gearing up for key electoral battles next year with special focus on Uttar Pradesh, the country's most populous state.

Jaishankar made the remarks during a session of the Raisina Dialogue's Middle East edition in Abu Dhabi on Wednesday, where he joined UAE Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al-Nahyan for a discussion on 'The World Ahead: Power, Purpose & Possibility'.
Highlighting the increasing pace of change in the global order during the conversation, the minister said it reflected both "long-term trends and immediate shocks", prompting countries to explore new partnerships and alternatives in response to their specific circumstances.

items.summary:
Delhi Police has registered an FIR against an independent journalist and others on a complaint by one of its officers alleging casteist remarks, public humiliation and defamation during a protest near Jantar Mantar earlier this month, officials said on Wednesday.
The FIR was registered under relevant provisions of the SC/ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act and sections 221 (Obstructing public servant in discharge of public functions), 356(2) (Defamation) and 3(5) (Common intention) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) based on the complaint by Assistant Commissioner of Police (ACP) Vivek Bhagat, posted in Connaught Place sub-division of New Delhi district.
Earlier, the independent journalist had alleged sexual assault charges against the ACP and an enquiry of her complaint is being investigated by the Crime Branch of Delhi Police.

items.summary:
Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels are attempting to build a new advanced medium-range ballistic missile system with the help of Chinese parts, according to a new report released Wednesday by a group that tracks the use of weapons in conflict zones.
The report by the UK-based Conflict Armament Research group came as the Houthis, in their ongoing war with Saudi Arabia, are demonstrating remarkable ability to wreak havoc on one of the Middle East's best-equipped militaries.
The weaponry under development could help the group more precisely target the Saudis and Israel. By turning to China, it also appears to be a sign of increasing independence.
The rebels expand their ambition, an analyst says
----------------------------------------------------------
The Houthis have tried to acquire key parts from Chinese suppliers that could be used to make a version of Iran's Kheibar Shekan precision-guided missile, according to the report. The Kheibar Shekan has a range of roughly 1,200 miles .

Fed hikes ahead, but not just yet
items.summary: San Francisco: The Federal Reserve will probably need to increase short-term interest rates further to rein in too-high inflation, San Francisco Federal Reserve President Mary Daly said on Wednesday, but she also signaled there's no need to do so at the US central bank's October 27-28 meeting."We are more likely than not to need additional adjustments, but the timing of those adjustments to me is something we're still deliberating," Daly told Reuters in an interview. "I don't feel urgent that we have to decide with a limited set of information. I think we have the time that we need."Also Read: US inflation worsened last month to 3.7% in sign that prices remain elevated as midterm elections nearSeveral of Daly's colleagues have also signaled in recent weeks that the Fed is unlikely to raise rates this month. The Fed's policy rate is in the 3.75%-4.00% range, and longer-term borrowing costs are even higher, with some -- like 7.5% mortgage rates -- putting an increasingly obvious damper on demand in some parts of the economy.Daly said she feels financial markets understand the Fed's "reaction function," pointing to how traders responded to data earlier on Wednesday that showed consumer price inflation accelerated to 3.7% in the 12 months through September, a bit faster than economists had anticipated. The Fed targets 2% inflation by a different, but related, measure.Though the initial reaction was "robust," she said -- rate futures traders quickly piled into bets on an October Fed rate hike -- investors "calmed" after parsing through the data. Higher gasoline prices drove the overall increase, and underlying inflation, while still sticky, did not take a sharp turn upward."Definitely this data point suggests that the risk to inflation remains elevated," Daly said. "The risk to inflation has gone up more, but risks are not realities, and reacting on risk when you have time to make a good decision, to me, feels imprudent."Also Read: More expensive gas, semiconductors likely pushed up inflation in US last monthDaly said that the labor market's continued stability gives the Fed room to focus on price stability.But, she said, "why force urgency when you don't need to have urgency? Why not take the time to be thoughtful and deliberate? And we have more meetings ahead of us."Financial market pricing now puts about a 40% chance of a second straight Fed rate hike at the central bank's next meeting, up from before the data but no longer seeing an increase as the most likely outcome.

The financial services entity had earned a PAT of Rs 581 crore in the year-ago period.
Its net interest income rose 15.6 per cent to Rs 2,534 crore in the July-September quarter of FY27, up from Rs 2,192 crore in the corresponding quarter of the previous fiscal year, the firm said in a stock exchange filing.
HDB Financial Services' total income rose 12 per cent to Rs 3,188 crore for the quarter under review from Rs 2,851 crore in the year-ago period.
Loan losses and provisions declined by 2.5 per cent to Rs 730 crore for the quarter ended September 30, 2026 compared to Rs 748 crore recorded in the same quarter last year.

Citing an example, Misra said online car marketplace Cars24 used OpenAI's models for nearly a million conversation minutes a month through a customer agent that helps sellers list their cars, and it now reports that nearly 12 per cent of its lost sellers are returning because of it.
"The next phase... for AI is really going to be not experiments but actually driving outcomes," Misra said at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum 2026.

items.title: UK study visa refusals affect university offers to foreign students: Report
items.summary:
International students, including Indians, are likely to be impacted as British universities revoke offers to courses amid a clampdown on study visas issued by the UK Home Office, according to a media analysis this week.
The Financial Times newspaper analysed official data to find that universities are taking the step to withdraw offers to students over fears of facing a blanket ban on their ability to recruit foreign students.
Under the Home Office rules, education institutions where more than 5 per cent of prospective international students given offers subsequently have their visa applications rejected face the risk of being banned from recruiting them.
This tightening of the previous 10 per cent threshold is aimed at what the UK government believes is the abuse of the student visa route by certain nationalities, led by Pakistanis and Nigerians.
"Many refusals appear to rest on flawed, inconsistent and highly subjective reasoning, forcing universities to withdraw offers at scale

items.title: Fairfax-IDBI deal brings a Canadian cheer
items.summary: Mumbai: Canada's Minister of International Trade, Maninder Sidhu, has welcomed the investment potential between India and Canada, highlighting the role of Canadian companies, institutions and pension funds in India's infrastructure development, following the Union Cabinet's approval of the strategic sale and restructuring of IDBI Bank to Canada's Fairfax Financial Holdings.Emphasising the importance of bilateral investments, Sidhu told in an exclusive interview that Canada has invested close to USD 107 billion in India and sees significant scope to expand its presence across key sectors, including infrastructure, aviation, energy and critical minerals.Also read: Cabinet approves Rs 52,878 crore IDBI Bank sale to Fairfax arm in India’s largest financial-sector FDI"We have a great deal of respect for Fairfax and Mr Prem Watsa for what he's doing here in India. He's helping build airports. But if you look at the infrastructure needs of India, that's where Canadian companies, institutions, and pension funds are doing a lot." Sidhu saidHe further pointed to the opportunities emerging from India's infrastructure expansion plans, noting that the country aims to build 100 additional airports and requires around 2,000 more aircraft, areas where Canadian expertise could play a significant role."India wants to build 100 more airports," Sidhu said, adding that Canada's aerospace industry, along with its infrastructure and energy capabilities, offers considerable potential for cooperation.The minister also highlighted Canadian pension funds' participation in infrastructure projects, including highways in India, describing the two countries as having strong economic complementarities.Also read: IDBI Bank strategic restructuring to attract FDI, boost banking sector, says FM SitharamanThe Union Cabinet has approved the strategic sale and restructuring of IDBI Bank in a deal valued at Rs 52,878 crore on Wednesday.
