The caveats filed in the Bombay High Court and also in the Mumbai City Civil Court will ensure that they are heard before the passing of any orders.
Both the father and son moved the courts with their caveats on October 7, as per official records.
Srinivasan and Singh had filed complaints against Noel and Neville Tata with the Maharahstra Charity Commissioner, alleging governance lapses and irregularities at some of the Tata Trusts. Noel and Neville had earlier filed similar caveats at the charity commissioner's office, according to reports.
The caveat in the Bombay High Court has Noel as the caveator, while Srinivasan has been named as the caveatee. Singh has been included as an extra party caveatee along with lawyer Darius Khambata and Tata group veteran Bhaskar Bhat.

The head of the International Monetary Fund said Wednesday that the US and other wealthy nations need to urgently tackle mounting global debt levels that are weighing heaviest on low-income countries and straining the global financial system.
IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva said that while US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and other US leaders recognise that the federal deficit and national debt have grown too high, just trying to grow the US economy out of its more than USD 40 trillion in national debt would not suffice.
"At the fund, we believe that, growth, of course, helps, but it cannot deliver fast enough the necessary adjustments," Georgieva said at the autumn meeting of the IMF and World Bank in Bangkok.
"There is no magic," she said, noting some other measures would be needed. "You have to go in a direction of tightening that, bringing it down, bringing deficit down."

items.summary: New Delhi, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman on Wednesday said the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs' (CCEA) approval for the strategic restructuring of IDBI Bank will pave the way for attracting foreign direct investment (FDI), while the government retains a minority stake in the lender.In a post on X, Sitharaman said the government had supported the bank's recovery and was now enabling its next phase of growth through the proposed restructuring.Also read: Cabinet approves Rs 52,878 crore IDBI Bank sale to Fairfax arm in India’s largest financial-sector FDI"Propelled by Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi's visionary leadership, India's reform trajectory reaches another milestone today with the CCEA's approval of IDBI Bank's strategic restructuring," she said.The move will strengthen India's banking ecosystem and help banking services meet global benchmarks, she said.Sitharaman said the decision reflects the resilience of the Indian economy and the government's continued commitment to reforms.The strategic restructuring is part of efforts to build a future-ready financial sector that empowers customers, supports entrepreneurs and contributes to the vision of Viksit Bharat, she added.Earlier in the day, the Union Cabinet headed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi approved the sale of a 60.72 per cent stake in IDBI Bank to Fairfax Financial Holdings for Rs 52,878 crore, in the country's biggest strategic disinvestment since the sale of Air India and potentially opening a new chapter in the privatisation of state-controlled banks.Also read: FM Sitharaman ready to hear out stock market tax debateThe decision by the Cabinet Committee on Economic Affairs (CCEA) brings to a close a process that has stretched over five years, marking a significant step in the government's efforts to reduce its ownership of state-run assets and attract private capital into the financial sector."Once completed, this will be the largest FDI in the financial sector of our economy so far," the government said in a statement.The government and LIC will together hold a 34 per cent stake in the restructured entity.The proposed sale of a combined 60.72 per cent stake held by the government and Life Insurance Corporation of India (LIC) would transfer control of the lender to Fairfax, subject to the completion of the transaction and requisite regulatory approvals.

Delhi protests: DMRC tells SC no metro services were curtailed or cancelled
items.summary:
There was no curtailment or cancellation of metro train services during the recent protests in the national capital and the entry and exit were restricted in 45 out of the 303 stations, the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation told the Supreme Court on Wednesday.
The DMRC said over 85 per cent of metro network (258 stations) remained fully operational, accessible and functional for commuters.
In an affidavit filed in the apex court, the DMRC said the entry and exit were restricted in only 45 out of 303 stations, accounting for only 15 per cent of the entire network.
It said the entry and exit regulations were undertaken pursuant to the assessment of law enforcement agencies and in accordance with their directions.

The Delhi High Court on Wednesday sought the stand of the FSSAI, the Centre and the city government on a PIL raising concerns over the sale of dairy analogue/non-dairy products as 'paneer' to unsuspecting consumers.
The petitioners contended that while paneer is a standardised dairy product under the food safety regime, a non-dairy, analogue product contains non-milk ingredients and lacks the same nutritional value.
A bench of acting Chief Justice Nitin W Sambre and Justice Sanjay Singh issued notices to the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), the Centre and the Delhi government on the petition filed by Ridhima Singh and Avlokiteshwar Padmapani Sidharth, and asked them to file their replies within six weeks.
The petitioners contended that a person consuming a paneer-based product in a hotel or a restaurant has no means to know whether the dish is prepared using actual paneer or a dairy analogue.
They sought urgent directions from the court in view of the festive .

items.title: India's price pain meets double-digit villain
items.summary: Wholesale prices rose to 11.39% on-year in September, from 9.92% in August, official data released by the commerce and industry ministry on Wednesday showed, due to a sharp rise in fuel and power, food and manufactured product prices.A Reuters poll of economists had, earlier this month, estimated wholesale inflation at 10.18% for the month.Meanwhile, data from earlier this week showed that the country’s retail inflation rose to 5.54% in September 2026 from 4.83% in August, owing to a sharp rise in food prices, particularly vegetables.Also Read: India's retail inflation quickens to 5.54% in September from 4.83% in August, hits near two-year highInflation in fuel and power rose to 25.85% in September from 22.93% in August, while inflation in manufactured products increased to 9.76% from 8.37%.Inflation in primary articles, which include food articles, non-food articles and minerals, rose to 8.67% from 7.76% over the same period.The wholesale food index, which includes food articles and manufactured food products, recorded inflation of 8.66% in September, up from 7.05% in August.Among the key drivers of wholesale inflation were mineral oils, food articles, crude petroleum and natural gas, coal and lignite, basic metals, chemicals, textiles, rubber and plastic products, and electrical equipment, the ministry said.Also Read: Double trouble at the dinner table: When will food prices normalise for Indians?An ET Online survey of economists from earlier this month, showed that food inflation is likely to remain elevated over the coming months, with some expecting it to rise to 7-8% over the next three to six months. While fresh Kharif arrivals and winter Rabi supplies could bring relief from late 2026 or early 2027, uneven monsoon rainfall, El Nino risks and higher energy and farm-input costs could prolong price pressures.Economists flagged El Nino and uneven monsoon rainfall as key risks to food inflation, warning that they could affect Kharif yields and delay Rabi sowing. ICRA’s Aditi Nayar and ANZ’s Dhiraj Nim had flagged to ET Online that below-average reservoir levels are a concern for winter crops, with the impact on food prices depending on crop output and adverse weather conditions.Higher global commodity prices and energy costs add to the pressure on food prices.Elevated crude oil prices can raise farm, irrigation and transportation costs, while higher liquefied natural gas (LNG) prices can increase fertiliser costs. India’s dependence on imported edible oils also leaves the category exposed to global price movements, while higher freight, packaging and crop-protection costs could add to the cost of bringing food to market.In early October, the RBI hiked benchmark repo rate to 5.5% in first such increase since February 2023, with Governor Sanjay Malhotra flagging “it is clear that inflation and its outlook are not benign as they were last year.”The September WPI inflation data was released under the revised series, introduced in June with 2022-23 as the base year to better reflect the economy’s current structure. The new series expands the commodity basket to 957 items from 697 and includes newer energy sources such as solar, wind and nuclear electricity.

"We are open to all countries around the world as long as we get a fair deal, as long as we ensure a continuity in the engagement, and as long as the geopolitical situation does not deteriorate. items.title: AI skills redraw entry-level jobs map
items.summary: India’s IT-BPM sector is set to revive fresher hiring after a sharp contraction, but the recovery is rewiring the skills companies seek in graduates.Fresher hiring in the sector is projected to rise to up to 2.1 lakh in FY27, after falling to an estimated 1.75 lakh in FY26 from 4 lakh in FY22, according to technology consulting and talent advisory firm HAN Digital’s IT-BPM Graduate Hiring Outlook 2027.However, demand is increasingly shifting towards artificial intelligence (AI), machine learning (ML), data engineering, cybersecurity and other specialised technology roles, away from conventional entry-level coding and business process outsourcing jobs.IT Services players will remain the largest employers of the sector’s freshers, accounting for about 60% of hires, though growth now will be concentrated in AI-adjacent and specialised roles.GCCs are the fastest-growing channel, expected to recruit 28% of talent as they expand intake into Tier II/III cities. Pure-play BPOs’ share keeps shrinking, mirroring the shift from routine execution to specialised, AI-adjacent work.“The rise in fresher hiring reflects a structural reset in how IT services firms are building their talent pyramid,” said Saravanan Balasundaram, CEO, HAN Digital Solution.As system integrators and IT Service providers sign more AI, data engineering and AI-enabled deals with existing and new clients, the bench capacity reduced by layoffs over the last few years can no longer absorb the demand, he said. “At the same time, new AI roles in data engineering, AI testing, annotation and model operations are opening up at the base of the pyramid, where AI-ready graduates can be skilled and deployed at scale, while mid-level hiring in the four+ years band remains under cost and productivity pressure.”The shift is changing expectations from new recruits. As AI tools take over parts of routine coding, testing and repetitive tasks, employers increasingly want graduates who can work with AI systems, validate their outputs and apply technology to business problems.The skillsets that companies are hiring for are definitely changing, said Sangeeta Gupta, senior VP, Nasscom. “It’s much more focused on AI capabilities – there are new jobs that are also opening up with data centres coming up.”The traditional model of bulk hiring, six months of training and deployment is also changing. “The new kind of freshers companies need are AI-native,” she said.This change is also visible in salaries. Freshers with AI-allied skills can command significantly higher pay, indicating that employers are increasingly paying for specialised skills rather than graduate headcount alone.India’s Tier-1 IT Services players’ 2027 fresher model offers Rs 12–22 lakh for select specialised engineers in AI, data engineering, cybersecurity and enterprise tech as the premium shifts toward specialised technology capability, found the report.“This would never happen in the past,” said Gupta, citing Infosys’ plan to offer up to Rs 21 lakh for certain specialised tech roles. Entry-level salaries across ITeS meanwhile have largely stagnated at Rs 3-4 lakh for years.Recruitment geography is widening too. Bengaluru remains the leading fresher destination, accounting for an estimated 25% of onboarding, followed by Delhi-NCR at 17%, Hyderabad at 16%, Chennai at 15% and Mumbai and Pune at 10% each. Yet, Tier 2/3 corridors are outpacing metro growth, albeit on a smaller base, at 35% year-on-year.Coimbatore, Jaipur, Kochi, Indore, Ahmedabad, and Visakhapatnam are attracting freshers via local GCC centres and IT services players seeking lower-cost talent pools beyond major metros.

The flight AI2030, operated with a Boeing 787-9 aircraft, made an emergency landing at the Jaipur International Airport and was taken to an isolation bay for security checks, the sources said.
Assistant Commissioner of Police, Malviya Nagar, Shiv Dayal told PTI that airport authorities had informed police about the emergency landing of the Frankfurt-Delhi flight following a bomb threat.
Further details are awaited, he said.
Police sources said security personnel were checking the aircraft in the isolation bay.
One of the sources citing initial information said the pilot pressed 'Squawk Code 7500', which indicates unlawful interference, when the aircraft was in the Mumbai Flight Information Region (FIR). Subsequently, the plane was diverted to Jaipur, the source added.

Delhi government has made Aadhaar identification mandatory for consumers to avail the benefits of its power subsidy scheme amid a steady rise in beneficiaries and a burgeoning power subsidy bill borne by the exchequer.
According to official figures, by February 2026, the Delhi government's allocation for power subsidy reached Rs 4,037.63 crore. For the current financial year (2026-27), the government has budgeted Rs 3,500 crore for this purpose.
Power consumers in Delhi rose by nearly 40 per cent in the last decade, currently standing at over 73 lakh.
In 2024-25, around 84 per cent (52.3 lakh) of 73 lakh domestic consumers availed power subsidy in Delhi, which rose to 87 per cent (55 lakh) in 2025-26, according to official data.

items.title: China's exports surge 36.3% in Sep as pressure ramps up to rebalance trade

China's exports surged 36.3% in September from a year earlier, its customs agency said Wednesday, as pressure ramped up from its trading partners including the European Union to rebalance trade.
The exports data, which was better than what economists had expected, accelerated from the 25% growth in August.
High-tech goods such as semiconductors and autos have helped fuel its rising shipments overseas.
Imports climbed 31% in September year-on-year, also accelerating from August's 28.2% rise.
That resulted in a $133.5 billion trade surplus for China last month, widening from $119.1 billion in August.

A federal judge extended an order blocking the Trump administration from banning reporters for three news outlets from the White House, as the extraordinary case pitting the president against the media makes its way through the legal system.
US District Judge Timothy Kelly on Tuesday ruled that CNN, MS NOW and Politico are likely to succeed on their constitutional free speech and due process claims.
"Still," he added, "no one should interpret the Court's decision to suggest that President Trump's concerns about accuracy and fairness in the media's reporting are unfounded, or that the government is powerless when its true aim is to protect national security when classified information is unlawfully disclosed."

items.summary: Washington: An engineer at OpenAI has been charged with secretly installing a recording device inside a conference room in what officials said Tuesday was an effort to capture sensitive conversations about the company's technology.The employee, identified as a 35-year-old Saudi national named Abdulrahman Alfozan, was arrested Friday, a week after the ChatGPT maker discovered an audio recording device hidden inside a company conference room, according to a criminal complaint filed in federal court in San Francisco.Also read: Meta says its new AI models on par with OpenAI, AnthropicThe complaint did not identify the company, but the company confirmed in a separate statement that it had discovered a "sophisticated recording device that was hidden inside one of our offices," reported the finding to the FBI and fired the employee."We used our models to understand the device and where it had come from, identifying that a specific employee had planted it a few days earlier. We referred the matter to the FBI, and we're grateful to the agents and prosecutors who moved quickly to make an arrest. The FBI's investigation is ongoing and we will continue to support their work," an OpenAI spokesperson said.— OpenAINewsroom (@OpenAINewsroom) "At this time, we have no indications of this individual inappropriately accessing or exfiltrating model weights, source code, or customer data. The employee was terminated," the statement said.The complaint does not detail what Alfozan might have wanted to do with any captured communications, but the company said the device was sophisticated, designed to evade detection and featured advanced encryption and audio monitoring capabilities.OpenAI said it had evidence the employee planned to place other listening devices throughout other parts of the office building for the purpose of recording meetings."This alleged attempt by a Saudi national to steal sensitive communications from OpenAI was taken extremely seriously. Theft of intellectual property involving cutting-edge super intelligence technology poses a serious threat to our national security," Attorney General Todd Blanche said in a statement on X.Alfozan made his first court appearance Tuesday on a charge of using or endeavoring to use an electronic, mechanical, or other device to intercept oral communications. It was not immediately clear if he had a lawyer who could speak on his behalf. He is due back in court on Oct 19.The recording device was found September 30 concealed in toilet paper and inserted into a USB port on the back of a television in an executive conference room, according to the complaint.Though the conference room where the recording device was found did not have a security camera at the time the object was installed, closed-circuit television footage inside the company's offices revealed that Alfozan was near the conference room on nearly a dozen occasions last month despite not having any authority to access the space or participate in meetings there, the complaint says.The company subsequently added a camera to the room that last week captured Alfozan entering and checking behind the television where the recording device had been installed, according to the FBI.Also read: OpenAI and Anthropic fear a major AI crisis in the next 6 to 12 months. Here’s what they’re preparing forThe complaint also alleges that he used a productivity tool to make multiple inquiries about the company's building addresses, meeting rooms, meeting-room capacities and calendars.Days before his arrest last week, the complaint says, Alfozan left behind an unattended bag in a different room that, when opened by OpenAI personnel, was found to contain his wallet, identification and another recording device similar to the one placed in the conference room.

items.title: Flights to Saudi Arabia suspended until Oct 17
items.summary: Mumbai: Airlines have suspended flights to Saudi Arabia until October 17 after the kingdom's aviation regulator suspended operations at Riyadh's King Khalid International Airport, disrupting travel across the region and leaving passengers seeking alternative routes.Air India, Air India Express and IndiGo have suspended services to Riyadh, Dammam and Jeddah, with IndiGo also suspending flights to Medina, according to an advisory issued by the Indian Embassy in Riyadh on Tuesday. Akasa Air has also suspended flights to Riyadh and Jeddah until the same date.The disruption has spread to international carriers. Emirates cancelled multiple services to Riyadh, Dammam, Jeddah and Medina on October 12 and 13, while Etihad Airways cancelled Abu Dhabi-Riyadh flights through October 19 and services to Jeddah and Dammam through October 14. Flydubai has reported cancellations affecting Riyadh, Dammam and Abha through October 19. Qatar Airways has suspended flights to Riyadh and Dammam without announcing a resumption date. Gulf Air has cancelled Riyadh services through October 17.European carriers have also extended disruptions. Lufthansa Group has cancelled Riyadh flights through October 16, while Air France-KLM has suspended services to the Saudi capital through the end of October. Philippine Airlines has extended its Riyadh suspension until November 29.The suspensions come after an attack at Riyadh airport on October 10 killed Indian national Mohammed Yousef Ali and injured 11 others. Four of the injured Indians remain in intensive care, four are receiving treatment in hospital wards and three have been discharged, the embassy said.While operations at Riyadh airport have been suspended, flights at other major Saudi airports, including Dammam, Jeddah and Medina, continue, though they face disruptions. Saudi carriers Saudia and Flynas are operating some scheduled services, according to the embassy.The disruption is forcing passengers to check alternative travel options as airlines adjust their schedules. Indian nationals needing to leave Saudi Arabia in an emergency can consider flights from neighbouring Gulf countries, particularly Qatar and Bahrain, subject to obtaining the required visas, the embassy said.It advised Indian nationals to remain in contact with their airlines to verify flight status. It also said Saudi authorities would allow visitors, tourists, Umrah pilgrims and business travellers who overstayed their visas because flights were unavailable to leave without paying fines.The Indian Embassy in Riyadh and the Consulate in Jeddah continue to operate normally. The embassy has opened a 24-hour control room to assist Indian nationals as the situation evolves.

items.title: Blackstone readies $100 bn cheque for India
items.summary: India is the best performing market for Blackstone, president and chief operating officer Jonathan Gray told Sruthijith KK in an interview. The world’s largest alternative asset manager aims to double its investment in India to $100 billion, he said, adding that the sentiment on the country is still positive. Edited excerpts:From your perch, what are two causes for concern about the global economy and two for optimism?Obviously the wars in Russia, Ukraine, as well as West Asia, which are causing commodity prices to go up. Agricultural prices are impacted, and that has pushed central banks… part of the reason they’ve had to move to raise rates as opposed to lowering. That ties to my second concern–the rising cost of capital. Interest rates around the world are going up. We’ve seen 10-year treasuries in the US go up by 80 bps in the third quarter. In Europe, we’ve seen a pretty significant rise, particularly in France. This is really a combination of the war, or the wars, and the inflation caused by that, as well as concerns around government deficits.Also Read: Blackstone has $100-billion plans for India in 5 years, says COO Jonathan GrayAdd to the mix this huge AI capex build and what that is doing in terms of demand for capital. All of that will likely lead to multiples coming down a bit for assets. That’s the major impact.On the positive side, I would say two things. One is we still see a lot of economic momentum. In the US, very strong revenue growth at our companies. In India, strong revenue growth. The second thing is AI diffusing into the economy, and the productivity we’re beginning to see at our companies, which is pretty remarkable.On the AI infrastructure build-out, is this investment sustainable? McKinsey’s State of the AI report earlier this year said adoption is deepening, but enterprise returns are flatlining. We’re also seeing some concern with AI debt…Whenever you have a large innovation and then capital flowing towards it, there’s a risk that things go out of kilter. First off, the demand is just continuing to grow, and I would say at our companies, the returns on investment seem remarkable. They’re finding new ways to use this technology. We have a garage door opening company that’s using AI visualisation tools to recognise when the package is coming from Amazon, then automatically opening the door. They’ve created a $50 million business that they think will be a $500 million business.We’re finding use cases in legal and accounting and all these different areas, and our teams at times can find it difficult to get this deployed, to get the technology right. If you think about a classic bubble–telecom infrastructure in the 90s–the supply was built with leverage well in advance of the demand. It turned out to be excessive, and ultimately there were a lot of losses.In this case, most of this is being built out by the biggest companies in the world who have very healthy balance sheets. What we’re seeing is demand is running ahead of supply, and the supply of compute is constrained by getting entitlements, getting a power plant, getting turbines, getting chips, amassing capital. We have a fundamental shortage of compute, and that is supporting the value. Most of this is now being contracted by very large companies such as Microsoft, Amazon, Google.How does the firm view the Indian economy in the medium and long term?Start with the short term. Obviously, there’s been some negativity because the wars have driven up energy costs. There’s been some pressure on IT services valuations with concerns about AI disruption and the market was trading at a very high multiple here. We’ve seen the sentiment in India, people have gotten overly negative, (but) when you look at the medium and longer term, you’ve got an economy that’s growing at 7%-plus, a very young population.There’s a lot of things that give India an edge over time, and I see it as the fastestgrowing major economy for many decades to come. As an investor with a long-term perspective, we say this is actually a pretty good moment. As the market’s pulled back, that creates a better entry point for us. We take a long-term view. I remember back after the financial crisis, most investors were saying, “Oh, India, gosh, I don’t wanna do that.” We stuck through it. That turned out to be the right decision. This is nothing like that. But again, if you look at the long-term fundamentals of this economy–the rising middle class, the opportunities that will create, India’s opportunity to be more of a manufacturing powerhouse globally–there are a lot of interesting places to deploy capital.You mentioned IT services and pressure on the sector. How do you see that playing out?I think these IT services companies are much more adaptable than people realise. They’ve moved from just providing services to be AI deployment companies. If you think about most enterprises, it’s not like I could hand you Claude code or Codex and say, “Change your business. Make your company different.”You need a partner to come in and say, “This is how you’re going to change your workflow. This is how you’re going to do your financial reporting.” India, given its strength in IT services, is a natural to help bridge this world. I also think there’s a big opportunity in India in the infrastructure we were talking about earlier. We’ve got AirTrunk here to do hopefully sizeable things in the data centre space. We invested in Neysa, which is a neo cloud.Blackstone has had a tremendous run in India–you have $50 billion deployed here. What has helped you succeed? Well, it starts with the people. Amit Dixit, who runs our private equity business, Tuhin Parikh, who runs our real estate business, have been with us now for several decades. They’ve really been builders of businesses. They’ve started with things that are very small or started from scratch. They’ve decided to start with something small, add capacity to it, maybe do additional acquisitions, put in place world-class management teams, ultimately take these businesses public. We’ve taken 14 companies public in India, five of the six REITs. We helped create the REIT rules here, working with this government that’s done such a good job.What can you tell us about Blackstone’s road map in terms of investments? It will definitely be playing this rising middle class. People are going to travel more. They’re going to consume more financial services. Healthcare certainly is going to be high on their list. We’re developing housing. We’ve invested in financial institutions who finance housing. All the things that happen as you move from a country with a very low GDP per capita, and many of those people move up, they’re going to want to consume. Providing those services is really important. I think this AI build-out is critically important. I think energy, which is an area India’s made a lot of progress in. The Prime Minister talked about progress in the solar space. I think renewables are very exciting. The digital infrastructure, the data centres and compute are really important.You have $50 billion invested in India. How much would you like that figure to be?In five years, we’d love that number to be $100 billion. Now we’ve got to find great businesses. It could be in private equity, could be in real estate. We're going to be expanding here in infrastructure. We're looking to expand in credit. I think growth equity is an opportunity. I think there's more we can do in more sectors. As the Indian market grows, it really works well for our business. People in India don’t fully appreciate just how strong your capital markets have become. The stock market’s up five and a half times in the last 20 years. It is probably, after the US, the easiest place to list a company, and that is very good for foreign capital because when you think about investing money, and in particular our drawdown funds, we’ve got to send the capital back to our investors. So the fact that India has a robust public market is very helpful. It’s another reason we have a lot of confidence here. In August, we sold more than a billion dollars of stock in a company, Knowledge Realty. To do a billion-dollar secondary speaks of the scale of this market, that there is real liquidity, and that is definitely helping our investors. It’s helping investments here. And so even as the stock market has pulled back here, the liquidity has really been maintained. And again, I think the government is continuing to make the market easier to access, yes, for foreign investors.There is some concern that we’re seeing in terms of public markets in India. In 2026 alone, foreign portfolio investors have pulled out $37 billion... Public market investors can be fickle. There was a simple narrative last year, which is that India is an importer of a lot of energy, and energy costs are going up, and that made investors cautious. India has exposure to IT services—AI’s coming. Simple narratives get established and then as money comes out, the market obviously has underperformed. But the public market can fall back into love again too. If the earnings growth, which I think is expected this quarter to be mid-teens, continues, the revenue and earnings growth, then you’ll see global investors come back.When you market your own funds and products to your LPs, are you facing any pushback? What is the sentiment about India like among global investors? The sentiment is still fairly positive. Global investors recognise there aren’t that many global firms who have boots on the ground who are capable of executing at scale. They want exposure to private market assets in India, but there’s a relatively small number of firms who can access it. The currency depreciation has been the other headwind for global investors. That’s probably the biggest question we get about India. But I think there’s increasingly more and more belief that this story has real legs.You’re significantly invested in software services, data centres, AI infrastructure, healthcare. Any other sectors or themes that have caught your fancy? Well, definitely travel, the hotel business. We invested in a visa processing business, VFS. We think foreign travelers are going to come to India more and more, particularly as the infrastructure improves. The airports here- –most people who come to India for the first time are shocked when they see the first-class nature of the airports now. As the roadways get better, travel is an area. Definitely energy in every form that you can come by. And, manufacturing will continue to be important.Financial services certainly, because you have an economy where you’re just starting to get people into markets. More and more people, as they get wealth, are going to look to invest, save, buy a house.You’ve taken a minority position in Federal Bank. We’ve been hearing murmurs about other Blackstone deals in the financial services space. Is that an area you’re beginning to get excited about? For sure. We’ve had success with Aadhar in the home lending business, ASK in the wealth management business. I just think that’s a natural part when you get this sort of increasing GDP, increasing wealth. Financial services are something that people begin to access. The banking system, the stock market, there- ’ll be all sorts of things. The insurance industry offers opportunities as well.Between Blackstone, KKR, Bain, Brookfield and EQT, some $50 billion have been raised for Asia funds. Typically, a third of that tends to come to India. Are there enough quality companies and scale opportunities to absorb so much capital? The Indian economy is now over $4 trillion. The stock market is over $5 trillion. When you think about those as the denominator, as the potential pool of investable assets, this is a place that can absorb a fair amount of capital, certainly relative to the amount of money raised in other parts of the world. I would say we are constantly pushing our teams to find new things here, but we haven’t found that we’ve had to compromise the bar.Globally, private credit has had a few challenges over the last few years. Are you seeing challenges ease up? What’s interesting is there was all this noise around private credit, and yet we haven’t seen what these sort of town criers of private credit doom were predicting, which was mass defaults and all these issues. Had they come out and said, “You know, you were operating in an environment two or three years ago where rates were really elevated, spreads were high, and there were no losses, and returns we think are going to come down a bit,” that would’ve been a very credible criticism. Instead, you’ve got a lot of noise and it led investors to say, “Whoa, I’m concerned” and it led to redemptions. I think the reality will be different, and we’ll see that wave ebb.I think there was some moderation in returns. But these products are remarkably resilient because they’re generally lowly leveraged, and they made low loan-to-value loans themselves. You’ll continue to see private credit, both on the investment and non-investment grade side, continue to take a lot of share.You love running in New York’s Central Park. Do you plan to run in India? Yes, I do plan on running in India. When you’re traveling the world, there’s no better way to see a place than to do it on foot. Right? And so, to wake up in Delhi or Mumbai or Tokyo or Brussels or wherever you are in the world, that to me is always a nice thing to do, run along the water somewhere

items.title: Let rupee find its own level: Uday Kotak
items.summary: Indian rupee should be allowed to find its own level, Uday Kotak, Founder & Director, Kotak Mahindra Bank said on Tuesday, asserting that the underlying strength of the Indian economy will reflect in the currency over time.Speaking at theBloomberg New Economy Forum 2026, he said, "My personal view is we should let the rupee find its own level, and over time, the true strength of the economy will play out."The billionaire also emphasised the importance of allowing market forces to determine currency levels without creating expectations about a particular rate that policymakers might seek to defend.Also read: 'If you can't beat them, join them': Uday Kotak backs Chinese investment in IndiaKotak said the situation should serve as an important signal for India to strengthen its competitiveness, improve efficiency and self-reliance, and invest more in research and innovation.A market practitioner, Kotak said, understands what works in financial markets. "Keeping investors uncertain about the level policymakers may be trying to justify can help prevent markets from anticipating official interventions.""My view is a practitioner has the ability of speaking what is going to be effective in markets," he said, adding that policymakers should avoid giving markets a specific level to speculate on.The recent pressure on the rupee was driven more by portfolio investment outflows than by the current account. The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) over the weekend announced a slew of measures to stem rupee fall.In a latest move, the central bank announced the creation of a special window for oil marketing companies, which is set to take the dollar demand away from the spot market and tightened rules governing forex derivatives trades to curb speculative bets against the rupee.Following the RBI measures, the Indian rupee strengthened for the third straight session on Tuesday and appreciated 40 paise to close at 95.38 (provisional) against the US dollar.(With inputs from agencies)

items.title: Shah counters RaGa's SIR claims with ballot polls
Fighting to restore democracy in India: Rahul
items.summary: New Delhi: Lok Sabha Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha and Congress MP Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday said the INDIA bloc's protest against alleged electoral irregularities had a singular objective of restoring democracy in the country.Addressing the gathering after a high tea meeting at his residence with INDIA bloc leaders, opposition MPs and student organisations, Gandhi accused the government of undermining democratic institutions and said the opposition would jointly fight to restore democratic rule."There is no parallel protest; there is one singular protest, and the protest has one mission: the restoration of democracy in India. Democracy has been destroyed, the Election Commission is destroyed, the Constitution is torn up and thrown away. We are fighting together to restore democratic rule in this country," Gandhi said.He also said the opposition would challenge the government's decision to restrict the use of Jantar Mantar as a protest site for expressing democratic dissent.He said, "One method of democracy was Jantar Mantar, but now the government has decided that Jantar Mantar can no longer be used to express democratic feeling, and we are going to challenge that idea. It cannot be so simple for the government to decide that the Indian people will not fight for their voice."He alleged PM Narendra Modi as the main "architect", Home Minister Amit Shah as the "implementer" of destroying the Indian Constitution."The people who have done this: Modi, the main architect; Amit Shah, the implementer; and Gyanesh Kumar. They need to understand that the net is closing around them. It is not going to be so simple that you can destroy the Indian Constitution and get away with it," Gandhi said.After the meeting, Kerala Minister Ramesh Chennithala said the INDIA bloc and the Congress would continue their fight against the Election Commission, alleging that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar had damaged the electoral process."We will continue with the fight because Gyanesh Kumar has completely ruined the election process. INDIA alliance and the Congress party will fight to the last. One thing is very clear: everybody is united, and we will fight against the misdeeds of the Central Government and especially Gyanesh Kumar," Chennithala said.He also alleged that a file concerning Kumar's alleged misconduct and corruption during his tenure as Public Works Department (PWD) secretary in Kerala around 20 years ago was being examined by the state government."I received an application regarding the misconduct and corrupt activities of Gyanesh Kumar 20 years back when he was a PWD secretary in Kerala. We are going into the details of the file. In the file, it is very clear that he is involved in various corrupt activities," he alleged."Now, the Kerala government has decided to unearth all these things, and in the coming days, after going into the details, we will take a strong view on these corrupt activities of Gyanesh Kumar. It is already with the Director and the Anti-Corruption Bureau of Kerala," Chennithala added.

items.title: NASA's Perseverance sets Mars record
items.summary: WASHINGTON: NASA's robotic Perseverance rover has now driven farther than any other vehicle on the surface of any world other than Earth, racking up 28.1 miles (45.2 km) since arriving on Mars in 2021, the US space agency said on Tuesday.The car-sized, six-wheeled rover reached the milestone 5-1/2 years into its mission to explore if conditions conducive to microbial life ever existed on Earth's neighbor.In doing so, it is visiting some of the most ancient terrain ever encountered in the solar system."Perseverance's engineering hardware and instruments are in excellent shape with all redundant systems still available," Steven Lee of NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory in California, told Reuters."A recent assessment of all systems concluded that they are capable of operating well into the 2030s, likely beyond," added Lee, the project manager for NASA's two Mars rovers, Perseverance and Curiosity.Perseverance has exceeded the previous figure of 28.06 miles (45 km) driven on the Martian surface by NASA's Opportunity rover from 2004 to 2018. Both also exceeded the driving distances of any lunar rover.TRAVERSING JEZERO CRATERPerseverance, with its suite of scientific instruments, has focused on the Jezero Crater, a region in the northern hemisphere of Mars believed to have been flooded with water and home to a lake basin billions of years ago.The rover set the milestone in a journey toward an area called Idubi, through the region off the crater's western rim nicknamed Lac de Charmes.Its companion rover, Curiosity, rolls along in the Gale Crater near the Martian equator.Perseverance is showing no signs of slowing down, Lee added.Its mobility system mechanisms are being tested to show it can drive 100 km (62 miles) or more, he said, with the hardware to be tested to the equivalent of 150 km to 300 km (93 miles to 186 miles) in the effort.NASA attributed a major role in Perseverance's success to its self-driving capability, an autonomous navigation system called AutoNav. Lee said 90% of its drives are done autonomously, with no human intervention."Perseverance takes stereo images of the terrain ahead, generates a 3D software map, and selects the safest path towards a drive goal," he said.Another key component is the Vision Compute Element, a fast co-processor computer that allows the rover to process images and run its self-driving software very quickly, almost continuously during drives, Lee added.That contrasts with previous rovers, which needed to pause to "think" before each drive segment, he said."Perseverance builds on the 29-year legacy of our past Mars rovers - Sojourner, Spirit, Opportunity and Curiosity - each incorporating prior lessons and improving our ability to drive on another world," Lee said.POTENTIAL BIOSIGNATURELee said the rover's biggest achievement was almost certainly its discovery, unveiled last year, of a potential biosignature, or possible sign of ancient microbial life.This was found in reddish rock believed to have formed 3.2 billion to 3.8 billion years ago in a river channel feeding the lake that once filled Jezero Crater.The Lac de Charmes terrain, Lee said, may yield clues to early planetary geological processes, such as the effects of large meteorite impacts. Jezero Crater was formed by such an impact early in Martian history.Lee cited orbital evidence that some areas of the rim were once hydrothermal systems with warm or hot groundwater."These areas may once have provided a warm, watery subsurface environment conducive to life," he added. "Indeed, some paleontologists hypothesize that life on Earth began in such environments."The rover's original mission envisaged just 12.4 miles (20 km) of driving. NASA recently approved an extension of its mission to explore the crater rim until roughly the end of 2028.The rover's plutonium-based power system is performing as expected, Lee said, adding it has "many years of useful energy still available."

Delhi Police has sought an extension of the deployment of 273 companies of the Central Armed Police Forces (CAPF) in Delhi till October 20, citing the possibility of protests by the Cockroach Janta Party and other organisations, sources said on Tuesday.
In a letter to the Union Ministry of Home Affairs, police requested that the deployment, which was scheduled to end on Monday, be extended to maintain law and order and deal with any potential situation.
"A total of 301 CAPF companies had been approved for deployment in Delhi, including 221 companies cleared on October 6 and another 80 on October 8," a source said.
Of the additional 80 companies, 28 had not reported to Delhi Police as of Monday, the sources said.
They said police have flagged the possibility of demonstrations at several sensitive locations, including Jantar Mantar, Election Commission, Parliament House and India Gate.

items.summary:
A preliminary magnitude 6.1 earthquake hit southern Panama Monday evening, according to the US Geological Survey, but there were no immediate reports of casualties or property damage.
The quake struck around 6:20 p.m. at a depth of 10 kilometers (6 miles) about 18 kilometers (11 miles) west of Rio Grande in the country's south.
The quake comes after two powerful 7.7 and 6.6 magnitude earthquakes and a series of aftershocks roiled southern Panama on Friday afternoon. They collapsed buildings near the epicenter and prompted evacuations across the country.

items.title: CJP announces protest in Rajasthan against 'illegal detention' by police
items.summary:
The Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) on Monday said it would launch a major protest in Rajasthan in the next 10 days against the alleged detention, house arrest and assault of student activists and social workers by police.
Addressing a press conference in Jaipur, CJP spokesperson Deepak Baliyan alleged that police in Rajasthan prevented the party workers from joining protests in Delhi and harassed their families.
Baliyan claimed that he was kept under house arrest for four days in the Kathumar area of Alwar district and personnel from four police stations were deployed outside his house.
Party member Gigraj Jorli alleged that police detained him inside his vehicle on October 10 while he was headed to Delhi to participate in a protest.
He alleged that his associate Surendra was also kept in illegal detention.

items.title: IMF raises India’s 2026 growth aim to 7%
items.summary: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) on Tuesday, raised India’s growth forecast for 2026 to 7% from 6.4% projected in July, citing stronger-than-expected momentum, resilient domestic demand and robust services activity despite higher oil prices.The IMF’s latest assessment also sets India apart from several energy-importing emerging economies facing a weaker medium-term outlook.Also Read: IMF edges up 2026 global growth forecast to 3.1% but warns economy is ‘vulnerable to setbacks from both directions’“India stands out with upward revisions,” the IMF said in its October 2026 World Economic Outlook, pointing to growing evidence of stronger growth potential.The IMF projected global output to expand at an average annual pace of 3.2% in 2028–31, below the pre-pandemic average of 3.7% recorded during 2000–19.It said medium-term downgrades were concentrated among economies directly affected by the Middle East conflict and energy-importing emerging and developing economies, with India an exception.134908208Domestic demand drives latest upgradeThe Fund raised its India growth forecast for 2026 by 0.6 percentage points from its July outlook and 0.5 percentage points from April. Its projection for 2027 was also revised upwards to 7%, up 0.3 percentage points from July and 0.5 percentage points from April.These upgrades add to a growing consensus among global forecasters that India’s economy is proving more resilient than expected, following stronger-than-anticipated growth in the first quarter. The World Bank and the OECD have also raised their forecasts, while other major agencies expect the economy to expand at around 7%.The Fund attributed the stronger outlook to resilient domestic demand and robust services activity, which have helped cushion the economy against higher global oil prices.“The region (Asia) has been incredibly resilient, even though its economies are net importers of energy and other commodities. The AI boom has more than offset the headwinds from commodity markets, with China and India emerging as the big engines of growth,” said Silvana Tenreyro, IMF economic counsellor and director of the Research Department.Tenreyro said the Fund had revised its growth forecasts for both China and India upwards, with India receiving a sizeable upgrade.China’s growth is projected to ease to 4.5% in 2026 and 4% in 2027, as higher oil prices, prolonged uncertainty and structural headwinds weigh on economic activity.India bucks weaker medium-term trendThe Fund linked India’s improved outlook to sustained economic momentum and stronger growth potential, supported by favourable demographic dynamics, a growing domestic market and structural reforms.Also Read: After S&P & Fitch, ADB raises India's growth aim to 7% but El Nino clouds food storyHowever, the brighter projections do not remove the risks facing the economy. Higher oil prices remain a vulnerability for India, while persistent global uncertainty could weigh on demand and growth.

Harvard Club clarifies on Delhi protest statement
items.summary: New Delhi: The Harvard Club of India has clarified that it has neither issued nor endorsed any statement concerning the recent protests in New Delhi and the actions taken by authorities in connection with the agitation against CEC Gyanesh Kumar.Rajat Sethi, an Executive Committee member of the Harvard Club of India, clarified the organisation's position while speaking to ANI."As a member of the elected body of the Executive Council of the Harvard Club of India, which is the official alumni group of Harvard University alumni in India, I wanted to issue a clarification that certain individuals have gone ahead and issued a letter remarking on and making comments about the recent protest and the detention that followed. I wanted to issue a clarification that this is not the official position of the Harvard Club of India," Sethi said.He further said that the Club's charter and mandate prohibit it from issuing political statements on its own behalf or on behalf of Harvard University."Therefore, this clarification is to explain to the larger audience that certain individuals who happen to be alumni of Harvard University have issued the statement in their personal capacity. While we respect personal expression, that is not a substitute for institutional representation," he added.In an official statement, the Club said that a statement reportedly issued by a group of individuals identifying themselves as Harvard University alumni, commenting on police action against protesters and the detention of certain individuals, reflected only the personal views of its signatories.It stated, "This is to clarify that the Harvard Club of India, the officially recognised alumni association representing Harvard University alumni in India, has neither issued nor endorsed any statement concerning the recent protests in New Delhi or the actions taken by the authorities in connection with these events. A statement reportedly issued by a group of individuals identifying themselves as Harvard University alumni, expressing views on the police action against protesters and the detention of certain individuals, represents the personal views of its signatories alone."The Club said the statement should not be construed as its official position or as an institutional endorsement."It should not be construed as reflecting the official position, views, or institutional endorsement of the Harvard Club of India, the statement read.The Harvard Club of India said its governing bylaws do not authorise individuals or groups to make political statements or express positions on behalf of the Club or Harvard University.The Club reiterated its commitment to maintaining a clear distinction between individual expression and official institutional representation.

items.title: Investors shrug off bear party, put big money into equity mutual funds
items.summary: Mumbai: Equity mutual fund inflows hit a five-month high in September, with investors pouring money into small- and mid-cap schemes despite a weak equity market backdrop and sustained foreign investor selling. Debt funds, however, witnessed outflows, led by redemptions from liquid and money market schemes by companies for advance tax payments, partly resulting in the mutual fund industry posting outflows during the month.Net inflows into equity schemes rose nearly 31% from the prior month to ₹38,306.55 crore in September, extending the momentum seen in August when investments increased nearly 19%, according to data from the Association of Mutual Funds in India. With September's inflows, equity funds have now recorded net inflows for 67 consecutive months.Contributions under monthly systematic investment plans (SIPs) hit a monthly record at ₹32,490 crore in September, up from ₹32,297 crore in August. SIP assets under management rose to ₹17.86 lakh crore.134905091The strong inflows came even as both the Sensex and Nifty indexes declined about 6% during the month on concerns over rising crude oil prices, higher US bond yields and continued selling by foreign portfolio investors.Among equity categories, small-cap funds attracted the highest inflows at ₹9,038.57 crore, followed by mid-cap at ₹7,834.84 crore. Together, the two segments accounted for about 44% of the total inflows into equity funds. Investors continue to favour mid- and small-cap categories despite their relatively weak recent performance, said Viraj Gandhi, CEO of Samco Mutual Fund."The 12-month benchmark performance was mixed as the large-cap index fell 12% and the mid-cap index fell 1%, while the small-cap index rose 3%. Against that backdrop, September's equity-fund flows suggest investors were still favouring mid- and small-cap exposure despite their recent weak performance," Gandhi said.Flexi-cap funds received ₹6,701.80 crore during the month, up from ₹5,059.42 crore in August, while large-cap funds returned to the positive territory with net inflows of ₹859.47 crore after witnessing net outflows of ₹1,147 crore in the previous month.Read more: Jubilant Pharmova block deal: Quant Mutual Fund offloads Rs 190 crore stake amid Rs 800 crore fundraising plan; Abakkus buys 11 lakh sharesHowever, the number of systematic investment plans accounts presented a contrasting picture. Around 6.3 million new SIP accounts were registered last month, while nearly 7.3 million matured or were discontinued, resulting in closures and maturities exceeding fresh registrations by about a million.Debt FundsDebt funds witnessed a sharp reversal, with net outflows surging to ₹1.83 lakh crore in September from ₹8,127.32 crore in August. Liquid funds accounted for the bulk of the withdrawals, recording net outflows of ₹95,743.20 crore compared with inflows of ₹19,934.29 crore in August. Money market funds also saw net outflows of ₹50,846.21 crore after attracting ₹11,734.71 crore in the previous month.The sharp pullback from debt funds dragged the industry's overall flows into the negative territory. The mutual fund industry reported net outflows of ₹1.33 lakh crore in September compared with net inflows of ₹41,368.05 crore in August.Read more: HCL Tech Q2 Results: Profit jumps 21% YoY to Rs 5,132 crore; co declares Rs 12/share dividend"The decline was overwhelmingly driven by liquidity-oriented categories, suggesting quarter-end treasury adjustments and institutional cash-management activity rather than a broad-based deterioration in investor appetite for fixed income," said Nehal Meshram, senior analyst at Morningstar Investment Research India.The industry's total assets under management declined 5.1% to ₹82.64 lakh crore as of September 30 from ₹87.08 lakh crore in August, largely reflecting the sharp outflows from debt-oriented schemes and mark-to-market impact from the fall in equities.Gold ETFs saw monthly inflows of ₹4,451 crore, marking a 71% jump from ₹2,597 crore in August, as investors turned to the safe-haven asset amid geopolitical tensions.

items.title: India beats China by $192 bn in dollar duel
items.summary: New Delhi: India attracted $351 billion in foreign direct investment (FDI) for greenfield projects during 2021-25, more than double that of China, according to the Boston Consulting Group (BCG). India's performance marked a 61% surge from the $222 billion greenfield FDI it received in the prior five years. China, in comparison, saw a 54% drop in FDI in newer ventures to $159 billion from $350 billion in the same period, and from a peak of $514 billion peak in 2006-10, per BCG data.Speaking to ET, Nikolaus Lang, managing director & senior partner at BCG highlighted the Indian market as the biggest draw for investors amid a sweeping global realignment. He, however, stressed on sustained focus on infrastructure development, skilling and cost competitiveness for India to further enhance its manufacturing footprint on a global scale.Also Read: RBI steps in to support rupee as currency nears record lowInvestor concerns about China are steering capital towards India and other Southeast Asian markets, according to industry experts. Greenfield FDI in Malaysia surged 125% to $140 billion in the five years to 2025, in Indonesia by 34% to $133 billion, Thailand by 97% to $56 billion. Greenfield FDI in Vietnam (-12%) and the Philippines (-24%) slipped in the period under review.134901861Lang said amid geopolitical uncertainties, multinationals are realigning supply chain strategies, moving from an era of sourcing everything from a single supplier and the cheapest possible suppliers to dual or triple sourcing.Also Read: UPI MDR rollout may be deferred beyond festive season to Jan 1"So, from that perspective, I think India has a role to play because the industry is looking for alternative sources than the one source they used to have," said Lang. For India to attract more industries, the country needs to mobilise capital, have a skilled workforce and put in place a demand stimulus. "If you don't have adequate people being able to handle stamping, painting, assembly, mechatronics, and things like this, you will always struggle to localise," said Lang. "And the third is to really have a demand stimulus... (so) if the local market is big enough, I think then it's definitely something which is worthwhile."He said Southeast Asian countries like Philippines and Vietnam have benefitted from the 'China Plus One' strategy drawn out by multinational corporations in the aftermath of the pandemic.

items.title: Centre to set up high-level committee to address sugarcane farmers' issues
items.summary:
The Centre on Monday decided to set up a high-level joint committee within a week to address the grievances of sugarcane farmers from Maharashtra and Karnataka, after nearly three hours of talks between two Union ministers and representatives of farmer bodies in the national capital.
Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan and Food Minister Pralhad Joshi held detailed discussions at the Pusa campus with a delegation of farmers from the two major sugarcane-growing states. About 80-90 farmers from different organisations attended, along with state ministers.
With sugar mills set to begin crushing in the 2026-27 season, which started on October 1, farmers have sought a higher support price, citing rising production costs. They have also demanded that the minimum selling price (MSP) of sugar be raised from Rs 31 per kg to Rs 50 per kg.
In a statement issued after the meeting, Chouhan said the discussions covered ground-level issues, including discrepancies in recovery figures .

Officials in the know said the 12-acre ground, which can accommodate 50,000 people, can now be booked only for December 29, 30 and 31 this year.

The Reserve Bank's liquidity measures announced last week to drain surplus from the banking system lifted weighted average call money rates by 0.12 per cent on Monday, experts said.
The measures, including moves to increase the daily CRR maintenance limit to 99 per cent and bond sales through open market operations, will also help accelerate rate hike transmission, they said.
The weighted average call money rate on Monday stood at 5.43 per cent against 5.31 per cent on October 9, according to the Clearing Corporation of India's (CCIL) data.
Money market experts said high surplus liquidity in the banking system can weaken the transmission of a policy rate hike by reducing banks' dependence on market borrowings and allowing them to meet credit demand using readily available funds.

items.title: PM will denotify democracy next: Dipke on Jantar Mantar denotification

Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke on Monday slammed the decision to denotify Jantar Mantar in Delhi as a designated protest site and warned "ab poora desh Jantar Mantar banega" (entire nation will turn into Jantar Mantar).
A standing order issued on October 11 by Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar named Ramlila Maidan, Burari Ground and CBD Ground in east Delhi as the new designated sites for protests and demonstrations.
"They have removed Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. Yes, it's no a longer protest site as anyway it was turned into a war zone by the coward dictator. Ab poora desh Jantar Mantar banega!," Dipke said in a post on X.
In another post, Dipke said Prime Minister Narendra Modi could "denotify democracy" next.
"Today, Modi denotified Jantar Mantar as a designated protest site. Tomorrow, he will denotify democracy itself. The dictator's problem was never the protest site. It was the very idea of people protesting," Dipke said on social media.

India remains the world's fastest-growing major steel market, with demand projected to expand by 7.9 per cent to 172.4 million tonnes in 2026, the World Steel Association (worldsteel) said on Monday.
The country's demand is expected to rise by 8 per cent in 2027 to 186.2 million tonnes (MT), the industry body said in its 'Short Range Outlook October 2026'.
worldsteel said it forecasts global steel demand will remain essentially unchanged at 1,722 MT in 2026 before returning to 1.7 per cent growth in 2027 to reach 1,752 MT.
However, steel demand in China - the world's largest steel-producing nation - is likely to drop by 2 per cent in 2026. In 2027, contraction in China is also expected to narrow to 1 per cent, the Belgium-based industry body said.
India remains the world's fastest-growing major steel market, with demand estimated to expand by 7.9 per cent in 2026 to 172.4 MT and by 8 per cent in 2027 to 186.2 per cent.

items.title: Not my domain: CJI Surya Kant on Delhi protests against CEC, movement curbs
items.summary:
"Ye mera mudda nahin hai. (This matter doesn't pertain to my domain)," Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant said on Monday, when asked about protests against the CEC in Delhi over the past few days and the associated restrictions.
The CJI was interacting with reporters on the sidelines of an event to commemorate the 33rd anniversary of the National Human Rights Commission (NHRC) at Vigyan Bhawan here.
The last few days have seen protests against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar in different parts of Delhi. Over the weekend, the capital turned into a fortress, with massive deployment of security personnel, closure of 45 metro stations and intensive checks at the city's border points.
Thousands of protesters, including Cockroach Janta Party leaders and former chief ministers, were detained.
The CJI, when asked about these protests and the restrictions on movement, said the matter was related to law and order.
"Ye mera mudda nahin hai," he said.

items.title: RaGa expected to lead SIR showdown to SC
items.summary: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi is expected to lead a march, that includes parties from the opposition bloc, to the Supreme Court on Monday in a bid to protest demanding the halting of Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and a resignation of Chief Election Commission Gyanesh Kumar.He is expected to brief members of the media shortly, ahead of the proposed protest march.The Leader of Opposition in Lok Sabha had earlier announced that the INDIA bloc would take to the streets again on October 12, alleging that Delhi Police and Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) workers used violence against students and women during the CJP-led protests in Delhi.Also Read: Rahul Gandhi calls on opposition parties, civic groups, others to join INDIA bloc protest march on Oct 12The march comes on the heels of a protest-packed weekend in the national capital where members of the Cockroach Janata Party, student organisations and opposition political parties were detained by the Delhi Police over their calls for mobilisation at Delhi's Jantar Mantar.Gandhi called for the "Challo Dilli" protest march which is expected to get underway this afternoon from Connaught Place to the Supreme Court against the functioning of the Election Commission.The protest is seen to take place despite the Chief Justice of India, Surya Kant, not giving his consent to a meeting with the opposition MPs on the issue.Rahul Gandhi was detained multiple times by the Delhi Police last week, after the Indian National Congress leader entered the Akashvani building in a bid to reach the Election Commission of India. He was detained again the following day when he called for a march to Jantar Mantar after Congress President Mallikarjun Kharge hosted a lunch for Opposition MPs at Sagar Ratna on Janpath Road.Security remained tight in Central Delhi on Monday, with barricades seen at multiple locations. Metro stations in Lutyens Delhi remain closed till 4:00 PM. Security personnel have been deployed at Barakhamba Road, near Mandi House. RAF (Rapid Action Force) and CRPF (Central Reserve Police Force) personnel are also deployed along with Delhi Police personnel.Also Read: SC bars illegal detention; orders normal Metro, rail, net servicesThe Supreme Court on Sunday, directed authorities to stop illegaly detaining peaceful protestors and ordered for metro services to be resumed, while ensuring free and uninterrupted movement of people and internet in the national capital. Over 7,000 protestors including senior politicians had been detained by the Delhi Police over the weekend. Abhijeet Dipke, Saurav Das and Ashutosh Ranka - the leaders of the CJP- were also detained from inside their Mumbai-Delhi flight on Saturday.Multiple metro stations were closed on Saturday and Sunday while internet facilities remained unavailable around Jantar Mantar and central Dehi.

items.title: Nobel memorial prize in economics to be awarded in Stockholm today
items.summary:
The Nobel memorial prize in economics, the final award in this year's cycle, will be announced Monday by the Royal Swedish Academy of Sciences in Stockholm.
Last year, three researchers who study business innovation won for explaining how new products and inventions promote economic growth and human welfare, even as they leave older companies in the dust.
The economics prize is formally known as the Bank of Sweden Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel. The central bank established it in 1968 as a memorial to Nobel, the 19th-century Swedish businessman and chemist who invented dynamite and established the five Nobel Prizes.
Nobel purists stress that the economics prize is technically not a Nobel Prize, but it is always presented together with the others on Dec. 10, the anniversary of Nobel's death in 1896.
Nobel honors were announced last week in medicine, physics, chemistry, literature and peace.

items.title: Beauty comes at a festive premium
items.summary: New Delhi: Salons and services apps have doubled prices over last festive season amid sharp surge in demand for services such as dandiya luxe and garba glows to Durga deity looks and Navratri queens. Executives attributed the increase in prices to a combination of a surge in costs of key ingredients such as palm oil, and glass and plastic bottles and aerosols by 25-30% year-on-year on account of the West Asia war, pricing power and the withdrawal of input tax credit on salons last year.“As we speak, consumers are booking packages for new looks for each of the seven or nine days of Navratri and dandiya,” said CK Kumaravel, co-founder of Naturals Salons. “Prices have doubled over last year, since with the unexpected surge in demand, the industry is exercising high pricing power,” he said.Also Read: Festive cheer shifts beyond metros as consumer brands bet big on small-town IndiaOn Urban Company’s salon luxe, prices have touched Rs 5,000-plus, with services including make-up from global beauty brands such as Casmara and Mac.Since this is peak festive season with surge in demand specially from small towns, salons such as Madonna, Looks, Gitanjali and BBlunt have hiked prices to cash in on the season.“Further, the consequences of the withdrawal of input tax credit (ITC) late last year on salon chains, fitness centres, gyms and yoga clubs, despite reduction in GST slabs from 18% to 5%, are being passed on to the consumer,” said an executive at a beauty services platform. He requested not to be identified.“As salon operators and owners, we pay tax on equipment and raw materials. In the absence of refunds of input tax credit, our overall tax liability remains high and neutralises the reduction of GST on services,” he added.The West Asia war, which led to supply disruptions and spiked the prices of packaging materials, further hurt margins of the entire personal care sector. Crude-linked petroleum derivatives, and speciality chemicals imported from West Asia are key ingredients for cosmetics and beauty products.Also Read: Retailers, quick commerce companies limit sugar rush amid stock painHindustan Unilever’s Lakme Salon estimated in a report that India’s beauty salon market would reach $22.99 billion by 2033, at a CAGR of 7.85% during 2024 – 2033. This compares to a market valued at US $ 11.65 billion in 2024. The report attributes the double-digit growth the industry is witnessing to changing lifestyles, increasing disposable incomes, and consumers opting for premium experiences.Chains are also pushing their private labels on other platforms.At-home salon and wellness platform Yes Madam said in a statement last week that it has expanded its Korean skin and hair care range Sokora across D2C and e-commerce channels. Cofounder Aditya Arya, Yes Madam, said in a statement: “We focused on making the range convenient for everyday use … at home as well.”

items.title: Mutual funds close in on FPIs in Indian equity ownership
items.summary: Mumbai: Indian mutual funds are closing in on foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) in their share of domestic equities, with the ownership gap narrowing to around 230 basis points, the lowest on record.The share of mutual funds' holdings in Indian equities rose to a record 11.7% in September, while that of FPIs fell below 14%, according to NSDL data. The FPI share has declined from a record 20% in May 2021, while the mutual fund share has climbed from around 7% during the same period. In January, the mutual fund share was 11%.The contraction in the ownership gap is an outcome of record selling by foreign investors along with unabated purchases by domestic mutual funds thanks to the deluge of retail flows into their equity products.134880107"In every market, normally local investors dominate and the same trend is emerging in India," said Samir Arora, founder and fund manager at Helios Capital Management. "It is reasonable to expect that in the medium term local institutional investors will own more of the market than foreign investors."Read more: Weekly Market Outlook: Nifty snaps 8-week losing streak, but can bulls reclaim the crucial 200-week moving average?FPIs' total equity assets under custody stood at ₹66.18 lakh crore in September, the lowest since March 2026, compared with a record ₹77.96 lakh crore in September 2024, when FPIs accounted for around 16.4% of Indian equities.Read more: ET Alpha Wealth Summit 2.0: What do Shah Rukh Khan and SIFs have in common? Radhika Gupta explainsMeanwhile, mutual funds' equity assets stood at around ₹55.14 lakh crore, up from around ₹20 lakh crore in April 2022. The corpus doubled to around ₹40 lakh crore by January 2024 and crossed ₹50 lakh crore in October 2025."Over time, mutual funds, high-net-worth individuals and family offices collectively are likely to account for a larger share of the market," said Ritesh Jain, founder of Canada-based Pinetree Macro.The changing ownership pattern is more pronounced among Nifty 500 companies, where domestic institutional investors (DIIs) have overtaken FPIs. DII holdings rose for the 9th consecutive quarter to a record 21% in Q1FY27, while FPI holdings fell to 17%, according to a Motilal Oswal Financial Services note.Sector Ownership DynamicsThe changing composition of the Indian economy could also be influencing FPI investment patterns. Foreign investors, which have historically had significant exposure to banks and IT companies, are now looking beyond these established sectors.The decline in FPI ownership has been visible across several key sectors, including IT, FMCG, consumer services, realty and financials. But, the trend has not been uniform, with foreign investors increasing their holdings in capital goods, metals and mining, telecom, services and healthcare.A recovery in corporate earnings will be key to a return of foreign investor appetite for Indian equities at a time when Asian markets such as Taiwan and Korea are hogging the limelight, boosted by AI-centric investments."If earnings grow at around 14-15% annually and the currency depreciates by around 2-3% a year, the resulting return for foreign investors would still be around 12%," said Arora.

Leaders of Opposition (LoPs) in Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha - Rahul Gandhi and Mallikarjun Kharge - had written to the CJI for a meeting with him between 4 and 5 PM on Monday to hand over a memorandum, demanding an end to 'vote chori', CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation, halting of SIR and switching back to paper ballot.
"Response of Hon'ble CJI to the letter received from Leaders of Opposition has been sent in their official mail," a source said.
The sources said that the CJI has not agreed to meet the LoPs. They did not elaborate further.
Opposition parties have announced a protest march to the Supreme Court on Monday over their demands. The Congress is calling it  "Chalo Delhi -  March for Democracy" and said they would converge at 1.30 PM at Connaught Place-Barakhamba Road ..
